tasks.title: Implement logical-message merging and thread reconciliation
tasks.details: Logical-message threading per SPEC F2. Messages carry a durable thread_dirty job mark; every import, body reparse, and byte-identical merge marks the rows whose parent links depend on the changed identifiers, in the same transaction (markThreadJobsDirty in packages/ingestion). ThreadService reconciles marked rows in bounded newest-first passes, one transaction per row: parent from the single valid In-Reply-To identifier or the last valid References identifier, one holder links, none stays pending, and conflicting identifiers, self-links, duplicate holders, and cycles stay unlinked and ambiguous; subject and participant similarity never links, and holders in another account never parent a message. Membership recomputes with each link: the row and its descendants move to the chain root thread, a detached row starts a fresh thread, and old thread records remain for drafts and snapshots. SyncRunner resolves a bounded number of thread jobs per cycle after body jobs and reports threadsResolved, threadLinksChanged, and pendingThreads in sync.status. Implemented and committed in 6fd3fcf. Two later passes (2026-09-19) re-verified workspace type checks and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL set — all nine workspaces green, 221 tests, the sync suite running all five files including both thread suites — so no code changes were needed and no commit was made.

tasks.title: Build the recovery-aware mail action service
tasks.details: Action service per SPEC sections 7 and 10 in packages/actions. submit gates the recovery generation before the idempotency lookup (409 recovery_required, 503 recovery_in_progress), validates the account, kind, key, and scope, then commits the immutable action row, its frozen per-target work items (occurrence revision, observed flags, folder generation, modseq), and one action.queued event before any remote work; a repeated key returns the existing receipts and a changed payload conflicts. execute refreshes targets from the mailbox first: folder-generation and absent-target conflicts, no-op confirmation when the refreshed target already holds the desired flag value (SPEC F2), stale-revision and modseq conflicts otherwise. Every item claims executing before its remote call, the recovery generation is rechecked before each write, and observed state, the receipt, and action.applied commit together per item, so a partial bulk failure never replays a finished item. Restarts reconcile bounded pending actions per account and replay flag assignments only after refresh; an interrupted move holds unknown and is never replayed; a lost destination conflicts. dispositionRestoredActions holds old-generation actions (queued as conflicted, executing as unknown) so recovery can complete, wired as the admin command recovery hold-actions. Remote IMAP writes go through the ActionExecutor port; the CONDSTORE and MOVE implementations are T012. Schema: ActionItemTarget extended with observed flags and modseq plus a partial index on pending actions (migration 0004). Verified: npm run check across all 13 workspaces and npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL, 237 tests green including the new 16-test actions suite.

tasks.title: Implement two-way flag and move actions
tasks.details: Two-way flag and move execution per SPEC F2 and F4. packages/actions gains the writable mailbox port (WritableActionMailbox: capabilities, writeFlag, moveMessage) and TwoWayActionExecutor, the concrete executor behind the ActionExecutor port. Flags: when the session reports CONDSTORE and the frozen target carries a modseq, the write goes out conditional with UNCHANGEDSINCE and the captured sequence; otherwise it applies only the requested flag like a +FLAGS/-FLAGS store. Every write is read back before anything confirms: a readback holding the desired value confirms (covers another client having set it), a conditional write whose readback misses conflicts as condstore_rejected with the refreshed state attached, and a plain write that raced a concurrent change confirms with the latest observed state and no ordering claim. Lost or thrown writes, and an accepted write whose target left before the readback, hold unknown. Moves: IMAP MOVE only; without the capability the item fails move_unsupported (no EXPUNGE fallback), a rejected move fails move_rejected, and a lost move response holds unknown for reconciliation. The service maps the new conflicted executor outcome to receipts, records the observed modseq with each disposition so the next action captures a fresher condition, and expunges the source occurrence of a confirmed move while recording the reported destination; the destination copy still arrives through normal synchronization. packages/sync implements the port on the ImapFlow session: single-keyword stores with unchangedSince, messageMove with UIDPLUS destination mapping, capability reporting from the enabled set and the selected folder, dead-connection answers classified as uncertain rather than rejected, and a condstoreWrites factory option that lets the post-login ENABLE turn CONDSTORE on for write sessions while sync sessions keep reading with extension enablement off. Verified: npm run check across all workspaces and npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL, 255 tests green including the new 13-test executor suite and 5 new service cases.

tasks.title: Implement clean view and reply quote extraction
tasks.details: Done: new @mail-hub/content package wraps the pinned defuddle 0.19.4 (linkedom 0.18.13, turndown 7.2.4) behind one ContentExtractor with two derived views. Clean view: Defuddle extraction of the sanitized body, then DOMPurify again through the ingestion sanitizer, then the reader's sandboxed frame; an empty or failed extraction falls back to the sanitized original. Reply quote: Defuddle with markdown:true over the sanitized HTML becomes a Markdown blockquote; fallbacks are the plain-text part, then text read from the sanitized HTML, and raw HTML never enters the Markdown source (tag-like leftovers reroute to a fallback); a derived quote respects the Markdown ceiling with a bracketed marker. Every pass runs useAsync:false plus a refusing fetch override, so no implicit remote extraction survives an upgrade that ignores the flag; diagnostics are opt-in and reduced to removal counts and reasons, never removed text or raw HTML; EXTRACTION_VERSION pins the config for deliberate upgrades. Redacted corpus (Gmail and Outlook reply chains, newsletter, calendar invite, table-wrapped one-liner, nested chain, signature footer, short note, empty HTML with text, plain-only) pins Markdown and clean-view output in snapshots, with hostile-input, fallback, redaction, and no-fetch guards. ReadingService.readCleanView and the session-gated GET /messages/:id/clean-view route (CleanViewResponse contract) compute the derived view on request and store nothing; the reader gains a per-message Clean view toggle that keeps the sanitized original one click away, applies the remote-image policy to both views, and states the fallback. ComposeService.createReplyDraft seeds the parent quote through Defuddle when the caller passes no markdown; the audit event records quoteSource, never quoted text. Verified: npm run check clean across workspaces; full npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL set ran 19 workspace suites, 0 failed, 0 skipped (content 16, reading 10, compose 39, api 70); the web browser suites pass against the production build, flows 14 including two new clean-view cases and interface 11.

The replay controller stamps each record with the recovery generation observed at creation, replays pending actions oldest first through an injected port, and stops the pass when an item predates the stored generation. The session probe now exposes the current generation (GET /accounts returns recoveryGeneration from the control status), so a restore is detected at sign-in: earlier-generation work moves to review with the SPEC message, local text and files are retained, a draft rebases only after an explicit comparison onto the shown server revision, and an uncertain send replays only after the acknowledged duplicate warning, with a new idempotency key. The web app caches downloaded rows and details and serves them with an offline notice when the service is unreachable; the header shows one sync line (offline, N waiting on this device, syncing) and the review dialog resolves each item. tasks.title: Create Coolify deployment and backup procedures
tasks.details: Done: deployment and backup procedures per SPEC section 10. New multi-stage Dockerfile with two targets: app (node:24-alpine, postgresql-client bundled, preflight then drizzle migrations then API and worker through tsx, APP_ROLE all|api|worker, Docker HEALTHCHECK on /healthz, unprivileged node user, durable storage under /app/data/storage) and web (nginx gateway that serves the built PWA, proxies same-origin /api to the API with the prefix stripped, immutable caching for hashed assets, SPA fallback; MAIL_HUB_API_HOST selects the upstream). deploy/entrypoint.sh runs deploy/preflight.mjs (DATABASE_URL, UUID RECOVERY_GENERATION, 32-byte CREDENTIALS_KEY, https BASE_URL, writable STORAGE_ROOT) before migrating and starts processes directly so SIGTERM reaches them. deploy/backup.sh takes a consistent pg_dump custom dump plus the durable object tree, writes a sha256 manifest, and verify-backup.mjs re-hashes the bundle and cross-checks every durable sidecar (key, storage class, hash, size); restore.sh verifies the bundle, restores database and durable objects, wipes the lossy cache, and prints the seven-step recovery runbook (new RECOVERY_GENERATION, recovery begin, hold-actions, reconcile sends, auth recover, recovery complete; CREDENTIALS_KEY and RECOVERY_GENERATION stay out of the bundle). deploy/docker-compose.yml runs db, api, worker, web with pgdata/storage/backups volumes for plain compose or one Coolify Compose resource; deploy/env.example and deploy/README.md document environment, volumes, Coolify setup, schedule, sizing, and restore. npm run preflight/backup/restore wrap the scripts; AGENTS.md records the deploy module. Verified: npm run release:gate with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes (typecheck, 560 workspace tests, 103 permission tests, migrations on scratch database). Backup and restore proven on a scratch PostgreSQL server: settings and seeded durable trees survive byte-identical, both corruption paths (tampered object, sidecar hash drift) fail verification, retention prunes, and npm run backup plus verify ran inside the built app image against its bundled pg_dump. Container smoke test on the built image: Docker health turns healthy, recovery init works in the container, the worker unblocks without restart once control state is ready, and the web gateway answers the PWA, proxied /api/healthz (200 JSON with prefix stripped), hashed-asset immutable caching, and SPA fallback. Built with docker build --network=host (throttled default bridge on this host). Re-verified on close: all fourteen files present and committed in b9a5520, every deploy script passes syntax checks, npm run preflight reports each missing variable and exits 1 so the entrypoint stops before migrating, and the APP_ROLE, migration ownership, and signal handling in entrypoint.sh read correct.

tasks.details: Done: apps/web gains Playwright browser checks that the release gate picks up as browser-workflows (npm run test:e2e) and interface-checks (npm run test:a11y). A fixture server serves the production dist build with a 100,000-message fixture API behind /api, so a real Chromium exercises the shipped client without a database. flows.browser.ts covers keyboard triage (j/k/o with polite selection announcements, slash to search, mobile back restoring the selection), the palette contract (the chord focuses the input, word-prefix filtering issues zero network requests, empty results, nested choices where the first Escape leaves the choice and the second closes, focus returning to the opener or the selected row), single-key guards (inert while typing, while the dialog is open, and after the shortcut switch), offline fallback (rows and details from the downloaded copy, the header chip, recovery on reconnect), and performance (the virtualized list mounts a bounded window of the 100k scope; palette input focus lands within 100 ms of the chord across five runs). interface.browser.ts covers axe-core scans with zero WCAG-relevant violations in light and dark on the shell, reader, and open palette, screen-reader semantics (landmarks, labeled search, named header controls, live regions, aria-current, state text beside color), a visible ring on every keyboard focus stop, reduced motion (0.01 ms transitions and skeleton pulse), 320 px reflow with the long subject and address, 200% text zoom at the 768 px reference width, pane layouts at 768 and 1440 px, 44 px mobile targets on the icon controls plus the 24 px WCAG minimum everywhere, and theme switching through the palette. Three interface defects the checks surfaced are fixed: the shell now has a main landmark and clips the translated panes so narrow viewports carry no horizontal scroll, the mobile menu, theme, refresh, and reader-back controls keep 44 px targets, and a failed page-one refresh falls back to the offline cache on the first retry instead of the second because the failure path read a stale closure. 23 browser tests pass and the strict release gate is green with no deferred checks. Re-verified on close: the first strict gate re-run failed intermittently. Chromium maps the translated mobile panes' rects through float32, so the reader's 44 px back control measured 43.99999237060547 px and failed the exact >= 44 assertion (one failure in six gate-equivalent runs; the interface itself renders a true 44 px target). The 44 px and 24 px touch-target checks and the inactive-reader pane boundary now allow 0.01 px of sub-pixel noise; the reflow checks already compare integer scrollWidth, and the remaining geometry margins are far from their boundaries. After the fix: apps/web typecheck clean, five back-to-back test:e2e plus test:a11y pairs with zero failures, and the strict release gate passes every check (typecheck, 7 migrations re-run clean on a scratch database, 560 workspace tests, 103 permission tests, browser-workflows, interface-checks) with no deferred checks.

tasks.title: Run the release validation gate
tasks.details: Done: the release validation gate ships as scripts/release-gate.mjs behind npm run release:gate and enforces the SPEC section 12 definition of done before each release. Checks: type checks in every workspace; migrations applied to a scratch database through the deployment path (npm run db:migrate), counted against the drizzle journal and re-run to prove a clean no-op; the full workspace suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL required up front and any failed, skipped, or empty vitest summary failing the gate, so a missing test database can no longer look green; and the action-permission suites (@mail-hub/actions plus @mail-hub/api, carrying the recovery-generation gate, scope validation, and the restore hold) run explicitly. browser-workflows and interface-checks auto-detect their apps/web runners (test:e2e, test:a11y) and stay deferred with their blocking tasks named (interface milestone T015+, validation T033); npm run release:gate -- --strict fails on a deferred check and is the mode for cutting a release. Preparing the gate surfaced a real intermittent suite failure: cleanup with DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) fails with "permission denied to terminate process" when a transient backend of another role (consistent with an autovacuum worker visiting a freshly churned scratch database) holds the database; it hit two different suites in two consecutive full-suite runs. All 17 cleanup call sites now share dropTestDatabase from @mail-hub/database, which retries the drop for up to five seconds, and the gate cleans its own scratch database the same way. Gate result, re-verified 2026-09-19 on the committed tree (01bd460), the loop head: gate exit code 0, verdict PASS with 2 deferred checks: type checks pass in every workspace, 5 migrations applied and re-run clean, 432 tests across 13 workspaces with 0 failed and 0 skipped; 87 tests green in the actions plus api permission suites. Browser workflows and interface checks remain deferred because no interface has shipped; T033 and T026 are still open, so the strict release mode reports FAIL on the deferrals until they land.

tasks.title: Expose mail action routes and wire the F4 management actions
tasks.details: The @mail-hub/actions service is implemented and tested (T011, T012) but unreachable: apps/api/src/main.ts registers no action routes, and apps/web disables every management command with the reason that the server routes for flags and moves do not exist (apps/web/src/mail/commands.ts:83-85, apps/web/src/offline/port.ts:125). Add session-gated, origin-checked, recovery-gated routes for submit, status, and receipts over the action service; wire mark read and unread, star and unstar, archive, and move into the palette, the row commands, and mark-read-on-open; connect the offline enqueue and replay path; cover with route tests and a browser flow. Delivers SPEC goal 3, F4, and section 7. Done: POST /actions and GET /actions/:id are session-gated, origin-checked, and recovery-gated (the generation header feeds the service's gate before its idempotency lookup); the wire carries per-item receipts, and a move or archive must name its destination in the body. Search rows now carry each message's active occurrences so the client freezes the exact server scope. The worker re-drives incomplete actions inside each account cycle. The web app wires mark read and unread, star and unstar, archive, and move through the command registry with a nested destination chooser, paints confirmed results only after receipts (plus mark-read-on-open once per message), and queues flag and move payloads offline for stamped replay. Browser flows cover star, archive, move, and the offline queue-and-replay path. Re-verified twice on 2026-09-19 after the loop reset the status to doing: every workspace type-checks, the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 680 tests across 65 files in 21 workspaces with nothing failed or skipped, and the browser suites pass (20 flows including star and archive, the move chooser, and the offline queue-and-replay case, plus 12 interface checks), so the implementation in 05fafd0 needed no changes.

tasks.title: Build the compose and send interface
tasks.details: Done in 60a09c5: the SPEC F6 and F7 surface on the existing @mail-hub/compose and @mail-hub/send APIs. The draft editor (apps/web/src/components/mail/draft-editor.tsx) holds a CodeMirror 6 Markdown source (markdown-editor.tsx) with a sanitized preview through mail/markdown.ts, the identity and recipient pickers, attachments with their upload state, and the two-second autosave state machine imported from @mail-hub/compose/autosave through a new subpath export, so server modules stay out of the browser bundle; a stale revision shows both copies and asks which one to keep. Sends queue with the frozen base revision and a fresh idempotency key (requestDraftSend in mail/compose-data.ts); the send panel keeps queued, sending, sent, partially accepted, failed, and unknown outcomes apart from the Sent-copy status (mail/send-state.ts); a lost queue response stays uncertain and only an acknowledged duplicate warning with a new key may send again. The palette reaches the surface through new-message, reply, and send commands, and the draft list doubles as the outbox. The offline queue is now reachable: compose-data calls enqueueDraftSave, enqueueUpload, and enqueueSend, so the review dialog path in sync-status.tsx is live. The fixture API serves drafts, uploads, sends, and outbound states; browser flows cover each send outcome, autosave with preview, attachments, reply derivation, and the duplicate warning. Re-verified 2026-09-19 after the loop reset the status to doing: npm run check passes in every workspace, the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 706 tests across 68 test files in 21 workspaces with nothing failed or skipped, and the browser suites pass (28 flows including the seven compose-and-send cases, plus 13 interface checks), so the implementation needed no changes and this pass made no code commit.

tasks.title: Add the PWA manifest and service worker
tasks.details: The web app ships no manifest and no service worker: no manifest link in index.html, no serviceWorker registration, no public assets, and no PWA build plugin (index.html, vite.config.ts, package.json). The Dexie offline cache only engages when the already-loaded shell gets a runtime fetch failure, so an offline reload or an installed-app launch shows the browser offline page and the cached mail is unreachable; the app cannot be installed at all, against SPEC section 6, F9, and the F12 installed-iPhone-PWA requirement. Add a manifest with icons and theme colors, a service worker that precaches the shell and serves it offline while never caching authenticated API responses, keep the runtime fallback, and extend the browser flows to cover a cold offline load.

tasks.title: Fix the deployment startup defects
tasks.details: Three defects keep a compose deployment from working. First, the worker service in deploy/docker-compose.yml sets APP_ROLE, DATABASE_URL, RECOVERY_GENERATION, and CREDENTIALS_KEY but not BASE_URL, while entrypoint.sh runs deploy/preflight.mjs for every role and preflight fails without BASE_URL, so the worker crash-loops while api and web look healthy: no sync, no sends, no classification. Second, entrypoint.sh never execs the passed arguments although the Dockerfile defines no CMD, so the README backup and restore commands are silently ignored and the container runs preflight, migrations, and the API against the live database during a restore, exactly what restore step 1 forbids; exec the arguments when present or use an explicit entrypoint override in every README command. Third, the .dockerignore patterns .env and .env.* match only at the context root, so deploy/.env created by the README workflow (CREDENTIALS_KEY, RECOVERY_GENERATION, POSTGRES_PASSWORD) is copied into the image; add nested patterns. Also pass TYPE_SAFE_API_KEY and the cycle-cron overrides through to the containers, and make the worker-dies path in entrypoint.sh wait for the API and pass exit codes through instead of exiting 0.

tasks.title: Fix the send and draft-lock lifecycle defects
tasks.details: Three defects in the send path. First, queueSend freezes the attachment list from an unlocked read: loadVerifiedAttachments runs before the freeze transaction (packages/send/src/service.ts:296) and attachUpload and detachUpload never bump drafts.revision (packages/compose/src/service.ts:452-492), so a concurrent attach or detach changes what is sent. Second, local pre-submission failures (mime_missing, mime_mismatch, credentials_unavailable at packages/send/src/service.ts:484-514) are recorded as outcome_unknown although nothing was submitted; recordUnknown never unlocks the draft, only a failed outcome unlocks it (line 1084), and no sweep or edit path can open it again, so a wrong SMTP password wedges the draft permanently. Third, no path releases lockedBySend after a successful send, so sent drafts stay locked forever and deleteDraft rejects them with draft_locked (packages/compose/src/service.ts:722-734) while listDrafts keeps returning them. Freeze the attachment set inside the claim transaction or bump the revision on link changes, classify never-submitted local failures as failed with the draft unlocked and editable, and release or supersede the lock on acceptance while outbound references keep the uploaded files alive. Fixed all three. The freeze transaction now re-reads the draft upload links under the row lock and rejects with draft_stale when they no longer match the composed set, so a concurrent attach or detach cannot change what is sent (chosen over a revision bump, which would break the attachment flows of the web autosaver). Local pre-submission failures (mime_missing, mime_mismatch, credentials_unavailable) now record failed with the draft unlocked and editable; only genuinely unclassifiable post-submission outcomes stay outcome_unknown. commitAcceptance ends the draft lock in the same transaction that sets sent via the new compose helper unlockDraftAfterSend, so a sent draft can be discarded while outbound references keep its uploaded files alive.

tasks.title: Close the restore-window session and disposition gaps
tasks.details: verifySession binds a session only to the database generation (packages/auth/src/service.ts:303-306), never to the deployment generation or the control mode, so after a restore the restored service_state and the restored sessions carry the same old generation and a cookie revoked after the backup passes verification with full read access, settings reads, and passkey enrollment when the restored verifiedAt is under five minutes old; apps/api/test/restore-acceptance.test.ts:369-372 asserts this behavior, against SPEC section 10 which requires restored credentials and sessions to grant no access, including before recovery begin runs. completeReverification (service.ts:324-356) also omits the challenge-to-generation check that completeLogin and completeEnrollment enforce, and new challenges bind to the raw database generation rather than the control-status generation (startAssertionCeremony at 596, startCredentialEnrollment at 388). In packages/recovery, countUndispositionedOperations inspects only the top-level status (controls.ts:87-90 and 300-326), so an old-generation outbound row with status sent and a pending or appending sent_copy_status counts as dispositioned and recovery complete succeeds while an unresolved append stays stuck forever because assessJob marks its job stale. Make session verification respect the control status with reconciling limited to inspection sessions, bind reverify ceremonies to the control-status generation with the same check as login, and count unresolved sent-copy states as undispositioned.

tasks.title: Fix the sync reconciliation races
tasks.details: resetFolderGeneration applies any observed generation whenever the folder holds something else (packages/sync/src/reconcile.ts:118-146, fed by runner.ts:263-274 and backfill.ts:187-192), and the runner forwards only the observed generation, never the recorded one. Two overlapping cycles on one account can therefore reset a folder to a stale generation, and the corrective re-import then inserts nothing because importHeaderRecord counts the invalidated fresh occurrences as existing, leaving every message in that folder invisible until the next real UIDVALIDITY change; reset only while the folder still holds the caller's recorded generation. Also guard the expunge comparison in steady.ts:258-273 so occurrences with a UID above the snapshot bound are never judged (a concurrent arrival between fetch and comparison is currently marked expunged and lost from active views permanently), and contain per-job and per-folder errors in runner.ts:133-156 with bodies.ts:234-237 so one stale body job (not_found after a move) no longer aborts the account cycle, skipping thread reconciliation and the sync.status event. Fixed all three. resetFolderGeneration takes the caller's recorded generation and applies only while the folder still holds it, reporting already_current when the folder already moved to the observed generation and superseded when it holds anything else; the runner forwards both values, and the paths that find the folder moved under a commit (the backfill window commit, the checkpoint initialization, and the poll arrival commit) report the validated generation as recorded and the committed one as observed, so an overtaken observation never rewinds a folder. The expunge comparisons of the poll and the nightly inventory never judge a UID above their snapshot bound, so a concurrent arrival is no longer marked expunged. The cycle contains per-folder and per-job failures into folderErrors and bodyErrors counters on sync.status instead of aborting before thread reconciliation and the status event. The fake mailbox now keeps UIDNEXT from regressing inside one generation, the way a real server behaves.

tasks.title: Bound parsing and original-fetch memory
tasks.details: Parsing holds the whole original, every decoded attachment, and the sanitized DOM in memory at once (packages/ingestion/src/parse.ts:81-157 with service.ts:91-110; only hashes are persisted), and sync buffers each complete original in memory via fetchOne with source enabled and no size cap (packages/sync/src/imap-session.ts:164-177). Steady state also loads every active occurrence of a folder on each poll (steady.ts:319-336) and fetches an unbounded arrival range in one transaction after downtime (steady.ts:207-209). One oversized message on the 2 GB shared API and worker process can terminate sync, send, and reading together, against the SPEC section 10 rule to stream originals to disk and bound parsing. Add a maximum message size policy (reject or skip with an event above the bound), stream originals into the durable store instead of buffering them, batch the flag-refresh and arrival ranges, and document the chosen bound.

tasks.title: Handle offline replay failures and orphaned uploads
tasks.details: classifyReplayFailure treats a 401 as a definitive failure (apps/web/src/offline/port.ts:48-54 with packages/offline/src/sync.ts:210-214), the sync status never renders failed actions, and the retry entry point has no caller in apps/web, so a session that expires overnight permanently kills a queued draft edit with no screen ever showing it. Treat 401 as retryable after sign-in (pause the replay pass, offer sign-in, resume), surface failed items with a retry and discard path, and give the settings screen the same session-expiry handling the list and reader already have. Also make enqueueUpload atomic or reconcile it: the upload record and its queue action are two separate IndexedDB writes (packages/offline/src/sync.ts:314-320), so a crash between them leaves a pending upload that never drains and makes every later enqueueSend for that draft throw UploadsUnverifiedError, even after re-adding the file.

tasks.title: Fix the classification circuit and rule matching
tasks.details: Four defects. The deterministic rules compare sender addresses case-sensitively (packages/classification/src/rules.ts:67-74) although the input contract documents lowercase addresses and every other path lowercases, so senders such as MAILER-DAEMON at a mixed-case host miss the bounce and security rules and spend a Jev call the SPEC says not to spend. The 30-minute circuit cooldown is dead code (packages/classification/src/service.ts:552-571 with the constant at line 60) because counted failures are filtered to a 10-minute window, so the breaker silently closes after about ten minutes and oscillates during a hard outage while healthz still claims a 30-minute pause. classifyMessage never consults the circuit (service.ts:223-255), so the per-message entry point keeps calling the adapter while the breaker is open. And when the circuit read throws, healthz reports not_configured instead of an unknown state (packages/observability/src/health.ts:228-240) because the classification circuit union has no unknown member; add the member and report unreadable state honestly.

tasks.title: Harden the API routes
tasks.details: Five route-level defects. The app sets no body limit, so Fastify caps JSON at 1 MiB while the draft schemas allow 2,000,000 characters and the service caps at 1,000,000; a large Markdown draft dies with the generic 413 outside the error contract (apps/api/src/app.ts:7, apps/api/src/compose-routes.ts:103 and 199, packages/compose/src/validation.ts:14). Every scoped handler ends by re-sending the caught error, so a database or storage outage returns raw internal messages and topology to the browser (auth-routes.ts:78 and the same pattern in nine more route files); map unknown errors to a generic code and log the detail server-side. The public healthz route returns account labels, colors, and both recovery-generation values to unauthenticated callers (health-routes.ts:141 with 51-61 and 90-102); trim per-account entries to identifiers and counts and drop or gate the generation fields. The login and enrollment start endpoints insert a challenge row per call with no throttling and expired challenges are never deleted (packages/auth/src/state.ts:66-83), so the table grows without bound under a script; add issuance caps and periodic cleanup. And importFolders assigns roles without the for-update lock that assignFolderRole takes (packages/accounts/src/service.ts:331-373), so a concurrent discovery import can hit the partial unique index and surface a raw 500; take the same lock.

tasks.title: Make the release gate trust exit codes and keep its logs
tasks.details: The integration-tests and action-permissions checks decide only from the parsed vitest summary and never check the npm exit code (scripts/release-gate.mjs:200-215), so a run that prints a clean summary but exits non-zero (a global-teardown crash, an out-of-memory kill with buffered output, a failing posttest step) records PASS and the gate exits 0. The per-workspace test runner also uses the if-present flag, so a workspace with a missing or mistyped test script contributes no summary and passes silently. The log directory is deleted even when the verdict is FAIL (line 263), defeating the printed paths. Check the exit code of every spawned command, fail a check whose workspaces produced no summary, and keep the log directory on failure. Done 2026-09-19: testCommandVerdict weighs the npm exit status above the parsed summary for the integration-tests and action-permissions checks; the expected summary count comes from npm query --json .workspace (check 3) and the named-suite list (check 4), so a silently skipped workspace fails; the log directory survives a FAIL verdict. Verified with a shimmed npm for each failure path and a full run against a scratch PostgreSQL database (PASS, 746 tests, logs removed).

tasks.title: Enforce derivative version and audit-event integrity
tasks.details: Three version and audit gaps. bodies.sanitizer_version is written but never read (packages/ingestion/src/sanitize.ts:20 with packages/reading/src/service.ts:132), so after a sanitizer change every previously ingested message keeps serving its old sanitized row, including through clean view, with nothing flagging the mismatch; compare the stored version and re-sanitize from the durable original or mark the derivative stale. EXTRACTION_VERSION is pinned only by a literal self-equality test (packages/content/src/extract.ts:22 with test/extract.test.ts:20-24), never against the installed Defuddle version, so a dependency upgrade can ship with a misreported version; assert the installed package version matches the constant. And createSavedSearch and deleteSavedSearch write their audit events as separate statements after the mutation (packages/search/src/service.ts:359-407), so a crash between them loses the event; commit the effect and the event together as settings and corrections already do.

tasks.title: Check storage writes and clean repository hygiene
tasks.details: writeObject and writeSidecar ignore the bytes-written return of FileHandle.write (packages/database/src/storage/fs-object-store.ts:128 and 134), so a short write on a nearly full disk publishes a truncated durable object while the sidecar and the database keep the hash and size of the full input, and only a later full verification exposes the corruption; assert each write is complete and loop where needed. The .gitignore lacks data/ and backups/ although both apps default STORAGE_ROOT to a repo-relative data/storage and the .dockerignore already excludes both, so a local run against a real mailbox followed by git add commits every stored mail original into history. And AGENTS.md documents every package except packages/harness; add the module entry so the scripted IMAP and SMTP acceptance harness is discoverable.

tasks.title: Harden the transport clients and test fakes
tasks.details: Five items. submitSmtpMessage omits forceAuth while the connection test sets it (packages/transport/src/submit.ts:46-65), so a server whose EHLO advertises no AUTH makes nodemailer submit silently unauthenticated; set forceAuth and add a harness case. The transport-package fakes keep the buffer, upgrade state, login stage, and authenticated flag on the server instead of per connection (test/fake-imap-server.ts:47-48, test/fake-smtp-server.ts:58-61), so a second connection to an upgraded server mislabels plaintext lines and can turn the no-credentials-in-plaintext assertion into a false negative; adopt the per-connection session pattern the harness package already uses. All four fake servers accumulate lines and client-declared literals without a cap (packages/harness/src/imap-server.ts:957, packages/harness/src/smtp-server.ts:208 and the transport fakes); add a maximum line and literal size that destroys the connection. The plaintext-password assertion is vacuous because AUTH LOGIN and PLAIN send the password base64-encoded (packages/transport/test/connection.test.ts:219); decode the AUTH lines in the fake or assert on the decoded form. And the trusted-CA comment in packages/transport/src/imap.ts:29-31 is wrong: the ca option replaces the system root store rather than adding to it.

tasks.title: Fix the worker lifecycle and cycle scheduling
tasks.details: Two defects in apps/worker/src/main.ts. The malformed-CREDENTIALS_KEY path returns early after starting pg-boss and opening the pool (lines 97-103), leaving an idle process with no workers or schedules whose shutdown handler only aborts a controller nothing reads, so it ignores SIGTERM and hangs the entrypoint wait until SIGKILL when the worker is started through any path that skips preflight; shut the queue and pool down and exit non-zero. And the sync.cycle schedule enqueues a new job every 30 seconds with no singleton key or depth check (lines 30, 273, 346-361), so a cycle slower than the tick, which the initial backfill over many accounts will be, piles up thousands of redundant jobs per day and then runs them back to back; make the schedule singleton or skip the enqueue while a cycle is in flight.

tasks.title: Raise browser-test fidelity and missing coverage
tasks.details: The fixture server accepts settings and account mutations without the recovery-generation header and Origin check the real API enforces, and no route can return 401 (apps/web/e2e/fixture-server.mjs:230-238, 241-326, 348-351), so a client regression that drops the generation header, a path that exists in apps/web/src/settings/settings-context.tsx:121-123 when the generation is unknown, passes the whole browser suite while every production save fails; make the fixture enforce both guards and add a signed-out mode that exercises the sign-in path. The axe exclusion selector matches nothing because the reader iframe has no identifier (apps/web/e2e/helpers.ts:68); give the frame the identifier or fix the selector. The palette-latency check fails on the maximum of five samples against a hard 100 ms with no retries (apps/web/e2e/flows.browser.ts:452-475), stricter than the SPEC p95 target and a known intermittent-failure shape on a loaded runner; use a warm-up and a p95 aggregate. And add the missing SPEC section 12 coverage: failure and pending interaction states (the fixture always succeeds) and visual regression snapshots for the shared components and main flows. Completed: the fixture now runs the deployed guards on every mutation (origin 403, session 401, malformed generation 400, stale generation 409 with currentGeneration), exposes POST /api/fixture/session to flip a context signed-out, and serves the passkey login ceremony; the reader frame carries id message-body-frame so the axe exclusion matches; the latency check warms up once and asserts nearest-rank p95 over 20 samples; new coverage covers the sign-in path, settings and list failure retries, skeleton and saving pending states, and visual baselines for shell, reader, palette, settings, compose, dark theme, and sign-in. Re-verified 2026-09-19 after the loop reset the status to doing: the verification run exposed one more intermittent shape the baselines carried — the compose shot left the drafts list's wall-clock edit time unmasked, so any run outside the baseline's minute failed on a two-digit pixel region; the row time now renders in a time element with the mask covering it beside the footer, the compose baseline was regenerated, and both browser suites pass (35 flows; 15 interface checks twice across a minute boundary) with the web type check and the 83 unit tests green. Re-checked once more 2026-09-19T23:38:44Z after another loop reset: the committed tree needed no code changes — the web type check, the 83 unit tests, the 35 flows, and the 15 interface checks all pass — so only the status returns to done. Re-checked 2026-09-19T23:42:09Z: type check, 83 unit tests, 35 flows, and 15 interface checks all pass on the committed tree; no code changes needed, so only the status returns to done.

tasks.title: Fix the reader and settings interface defects
tasks.details: All five fixed. The Clean view toggle records the per-message choice in both directions, so a reader with the clean-view default on can still switch one message back to the sanitized original; the next message starts from the default again. The unified inbox no longer skeletons forever when the folder index read fails: useMessageList takes the folder-index error and surfaces the list failure with a retry, and while the inbox waits on a failed read the retry reloads the folder index itself, so the view recovers instead of re-running a query that cannot run. The offline fallback filters the downloaded rows by the active scope and query (new filterCachedRows in mail/view.ts: the unified inbox keeps rows an indexed inbox folder holds, an account scope keeps its account narrowed to the folder, and a query narrows by the subject, snippet, and sender a row carries), the offline notice states the query narrowing, and a downloaded set with no scope match shows the honest empty state instead of every cached row. Failed settings saves queue instead of keeping only the last patch: every failed patch waits together, a newer edit of the same keys supersedes what it queued, retry sends the merged queue in one request, and a success adopts only the keys its own patch carries (pickPatched), so an out-of-order response can no longer revert a newer edit on the display. Settings mutations carry the session-expiry path the list and reader already have: the save footer and each account card state the ended session with a Sign in again action instead of raw error text beside a retry that cannot succeed. Verified: npm run check clean in every workspace; the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 761 tests across 69 test files in 21 workspaces with nothing failed or skipped; the web unit suite passes 90 tests including the new 7-test filterCachedRows suite; the browser suites pass 39 flows (new: a default-on clean view switches off for one message, the offline fallback honors the active query, a failed folder read recovers from the list pane, and a session-expired settings save offers sign-in) and 15 interface checks with the visual baselines unchanged.

tasks.title: Harden backup, restore, and the web gateway
tasks.details: Four deploy items. The backup copies the durable tree with no garbage-collection pause hook although SPEC section 10 step 6 requires copying referenced objects while collection is paused (deploy/backup.sh:49-55); nothing implements collection yet, so define the coordination, for example a lock the sweep honors, before any collection lands. The database restore runs pg_restore without exit-on-error or single-transaction while the clean mode cannot drop objects added after the backup (deploy/restore.sh:66-71), so restoring an older bundle onto a newer schema rewinds the migration journal and the entrypoint crash-loops on re-applied migrations; fail atomically instead. The backup manifest and README claim the bundle never contains RECOVERY_GENERATION (deploy/backup.sh:69, deploy/README.md:166) but the dump includes service_state.recovery_generation; reword to say the generation in the snapshot must never be reused. And the nginx gateway sends no X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or document CSP for the PWA shell (deploy/nginx-web.conf.template:12-47); add baseline headers.

tasks.title: Harden action execution claims and readback classification
tasks.details: Done. A receipt from the claim that ran the remote write now supersedes the unknown interrupted hold a concurrent run recorded: the four executor dispositions in executeFolderGroup pass supersedesHold, and the commitDisposition guard accepts a still-pending item or an item holding outcome reason interrupted (restored_generation and lost-answer holds stay final), so a confirmed move still records its receipt and expunges the source occurrence locally. The post-write readback in applyFlags is guarded: a fetch that throws after an answered write classifies as unknown with the last observed state attached (ExecutorOutcome unknown gained optional observed; the receipt records it, the local observation stays untouched), per the F2 lost-response rule. Both defects carry regression tests that fail on the pre-fix code.

tasks.title: Fix the restore path's queue-schema mismatch
tasks.details: Done. The restore failed as shipped: the dump is whole-database and carries the pgboss schema, but the staged reset dropped only public and drizzle, so the replayed CREATE SCHEMA pgboss collided with the schema the worker had left in the target and ON_ERROR_STOP aborted the single transaction. restore.sh now drops the queue schema with the application schemas (DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS pgboss CASCADE before the replay). The replay rebuilds the queue with the jobs the backup holds, recovery keeps them disabled through the job gate, and pg-boss re-applies its own migrations on the next start; a bundle from before any worker ran holds no queue schema, which IF EXISTS covers. backup.sh validates BACKUP_KEEP as a positive integer before anything runs, so a bad value can no longer empty the bundle directory at the retention prune. README, env.example, and the compose file document the compose DATABASE_URL rule: POSTGRES_PASSWORD is spliced into the URL verbatim, so it must hold only URI-safe characters (openssl rand -hex 24; base64 output can contain a slash). Proven end to end on PostgreSQL 16: a backup of a migrated database with a live pgboss schema and one queued job was restored over post-backup drift (a new settings row and an extra pgboss table); the restore exits 0 and returns exactly the backup (queued job, settings row, drizzle journal, drift gone), a second restore is idempotent, a fresh-install bundle restores over a queue-bearing database, and pg-boss then starts and recreates its schema (version 42). BACKUP_KEEP 0, abc, -1, 1.5, and a blank each exit 1 with no bundle and no pause marker left; retention 2 prunes. The restore-acceptance suite still passes (4 tests).

tasks.title: Keep empty streams from destroying durable originals
tasks.details: writeObject renames the temp file over the final path before any caller inspects the result (packages/database/src/storage/fs-object-store.ts:155). The streaming path of stageOriginal then tests sizeBytes === 0, removes the key, and throws (packages/ingestion/src/service.ts:149-164). The rename has already replaced the durable original under that key. A truncated server stream therefore destroys the stored bytes while the database still references them. The docstring falsely claims stored bytes stay untouched. Enforce the size policy before the rename, or complete the object before it becomes visible. Also sweep stray .tmp-* files after a crash, because the durable tree keeps them and the backup copies them.

tasks.title: Correct send outcome and snapshot edge cases
tasks.details: reconcileUnknownOutcome commits the acceptance with the pre-send recipientResults, which hold accepted: false for every recipient (packages/send/src/service.ts:937-946). The send shows as sent while the panel reports no acceptance. Derive honest results from the verified Sent copy, or mark them unknown. A sent_folder_unmapped answer overwrites the recorded unknown outcome instead of preserving it for review. Recipient lists are deduped per list only, so one address in To and Cc receives two copies; dedupe across lists. The send idempotency request hash omits the frozen attachment set, so changed attachments can reuse a key. Per-attachment size caps exist, but no aggregate bound limits the composed MIME size. An empty Markdown body produces no text/plain part at all. Add the deliberate-resend path for a draft locked by an outcome_unknown send: the owner acknowledges the duplicate warning, then a new key or draft is issued. No automatic resend.

tasks.title: Fix offline draft replay and list overlay defects
tasks.details: Done in 1e07ad5 and re-verified 2026-09-20 against the code: settleSynced chains the base revision through queued saves of one draft during replay (packages/offline/src/sync.ts:542-561); the app shell retires flagPatches and movedAside overlays when a server read rises (apps/web/src/components/mail/app-shell.tsx); the list keeps stale rows visible during same-identity reloads through the refreshing and serverReadId state (apps/web/src/mail/data.ts); the send panel guards double submits with the sendInFlight ref and sending state (apps/web/src/components/mail/draft-editor.tsx:146); and the API client sets REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS so a stalled connection falls back to the offline cache (apps/web/src/lib/api.ts). The loop had reset the status; this pass made no code changes. Original defects: queued draft-saves freeze the base revision at enqueue time, and the autosaver advances its revision only on a saved outcome (apps/web/src/mail/compose-data.ts:596). The second offline edit replays against the revision the first edit moved. The server rejects draft_stale (packages/compose/src/service.ts:309), so every save after the first lands in manual review although no competing change exists. Chain the base revision through queued saves of one draft during replay (settleSynced, packages/offline/src/sync.ts:523-551). The flagPatches and movedAside overlays are only added, never cleared on a fresh server read (apps/web/src/components/mail/app-shell.tsx:120-198). An archived message stays hidden from All Mail and search for the whole session, against the SPEC rule that nothing is hidden. A single-page reload blanks the list to a skeleton instead of keeping stale rows (apps/web/src/mail/data.ts:519-527). The send action lacks a double-submit guard. The API client sets no request timeout, so a stalled connection never falls back to the offline cache (apps/web/src/lib/api.ts).

tasks.title: Fix sync scale and retry defects
tasks.details: The due-ness reads max(at) per folder and event type over an index that does not cover at (packages/sync/src/store.ts:98-114). Measured on 1M events: 52.6 ms per check; with a covering index (type, entity_id, at desc): 0.094 ms. Every cycle pays this for every folder, and the events table is never pruned. Add the covering index or store last_polled_at on folders. A body job whose stream aborts on the size policy, or whose original fails to parse, retries forever with no backoff and no event. The row stays fetched_body = false and each cycle re-downloads up to 50 MiB; the parse case re-downloads bytes already staged (packages/sync/src/bodies.ts:199-229). Route a size abort to skipOversized and record a bounded error state for parse failures. markExpunges and the nightly inventory pass the whole absent set to one inArray (packages/sync/src/steady.ts:329-341, reconcile.ts:277-289). More than 65535 absent rows exceeds the bind limit, the poll throws every cycle, and the folder stops syncing. Mark expunges in bounded slices. Also: enable condstoreWrites for the action executor session so the CONDSTORE write path is not dead code (packages/sync/src/imap-session.ts:37-70); batch the per-record markThreadJobsDirty calls inside the import transaction (store.ts:193-195); batch the flag-refresh UPDATE and guard it with expunged_at is null (steady.ts:427-438); page the occurrence reads in markExpunges and the inventory; prune detached thread rows nothing references; and give the runner a logger so contained folder and body failures leave a diagnostic.
tasks.notes:
Done. Seven regression tests, each proven to fail on the pre-fix code (git stash of the touched source, test run, restore):
- Covering index: migration 0008 replaces events_type_entity_id_idx with events_type_entity_id_at_idx (type, entity_id, at desc). Test asserts the index definition and the old index gone; pre-fix (journal stashed) the query returns 0 rows.
- Stream size crossing: fetchBody routes a message_too_large IngestionError from stageOriginal to skipOversized with the crossing byte count; IngestionError now carries sizeBytes. Pre-fix the error propagated out of fetchBody.
- Parse failure: a parse_failed IngestionError from applyStagedOriginal sets messages.body_failed_at and records one message.body_failed event whose payload holds the reason code only, never parser text; the row stops qualifying as a body job. Pre-fix the error propagated out of fetchBody.
- Flag refresh guard: the batched UPDATE skips occurrences whose expunged_at or invalidated_at moved between the page read and the commit. Pre-fix the test observed flagsChanged 1 written onto an expunged row; post-fix 0 with the row untouched.
- Bind limit: markExpunges pages occurrence reads keyset-style and updates in OCCURRENCE_SLICE (5000) slices; the nightly inventory does the same. Test seeds 65,536 occurrences; pre-fix the single inArray update failed with 65,536 bound parameters, post-fix all 65,536 mark expunged.
- Runner logger: contained folder and body failures log one warn line naming the folder or job, without credentials or content. Pre-fix the collecting logger stayed empty.
- Thread pruning: reconcileAccount deletes thread rows nothing references (messages, drafts, outbound_messages) after each pass, bounded at 500, and reports threadsPruned; the reconciliation event fires for a prune-only pass. Pre-fix the summary field was undefined and the orphan row survived.
Two changes are proven by inspection, not by a fail-pre-fix test: the batched markThreadJobsDirty calls (backfill, arrivals, repairs) are a performance-only rewrite with identical marking semantics, and the worker now opens its account session with condstoreWrites: true, which is deployment wiring (the factory option and the CONDSTORE write path are covered by the harness suite).
Test-seeding note: the 65,536-row occurrence seed goes in as eight sliced statements. One giant statement queues three referential checks per row in a single after-trigger batch, which this machine's PostgreSQL grinds through for minutes; eight slices finish in seconds.
Verification: sync 70/70, ingestion 26/26, database 27/27, worker and api typechecks clean.

tasks.title: Fix the Jev adapter timeout and harness fidelity
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. The adapter timer now stays armed until the payload is parsed, so a stalled response body fails as a timeout instead of hanging ask(); the abort state of the signal, not the error shape, decides, because undici raises a DOMException no name check matches (packages/classification/src/adapter.ts). The harness IMAP server answers work commands with BAD before authentication, the way RFC 3501 gates them, and fault delay timers are registered on the connection state so dropConnection clears them; the SMTP server checks the decoded username of AUTH LOGIN (a correct password under a wrong username stays a refusal) and clears a delayed final answer when the connection closes. Every regression test was verified to fail on the pre-fix code: the stalled body hung past the deadline, LIST answered OK before login, the wrong-username login got 235, the closed IMAP connection still wrote the flag, and the exit-probe child stayed alive on the uncleared answer timer. On the last claim: classifyMessage cannot throw RangeError as described, because the pre-T070 code already clamped its slice with Math.max(0, ...) and String.slice never throws on a past-end index; the unbounded-header defect that could push composition out of bounds was real and is fixed and tested by T070. A pathological-inputs test now pins the composer against empty fields, lone surrogates, and oversized fields.

tasks.title: Close search, content, and route gaps
tasks.details: The from: operator matches the display name as well as the address, so a spoofed display name matches a from: sender filter (packages/search/src). A query with a dangling quote is accepted and silently matched as literals; reject it. The total on an out-of-range page reports the full count instead of clamping. One Defuddle diagnostic path console.logs extracted message content, against SPEC section 9, which forbids message bodies in logs; remove the leak first. The account routes validate ids with a loose pattern, so a malformed UUID reaches the database layer and surfaces a 500. The action refresh reads the folder generation after the work item is frozen; guard the write when uidvalidity changed in between. The bootstrap command can issue two enrollment grants under a race; make the grant issue idempotent.
tasks.notes:
Done. Six code changes, five proven to fail on the pre-fix code (git stash of the touched source, test run, restore); one ledger item was already absent from the tree.
- from:/to: now match addresses, not display names: three anchored LIKE arms (suffix of the final address, fragment before an @, full address before the next participant's space) replace the contains match. Test seeds a spoofed display name and asserts the bait never matches while local part, domain, full address, and mid-list recipient still do. Pre-fix failure: 'expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []'.
- parseSearchQuery rejects a query with an odd number of double quotes (invalid_query, 'closing quote'). Pre-fix the quote vanished into free text or rode inside an operator value. Pre-fix failure: the new query.test.ts case did not throw.
- Out-of-range page totals: the ledger said the full count was reported; the observed defect was the reverse - the window total rides returned rows, so a page past the last match collapsed to 0 and read as an empty mailbox. An empty page at offset > 0 now re-counts the same joins and conditions and reports the true total; a genuine zero stays zero. Pre-fix failure: 'expected +0 to be 1'.
- Route id validation: the loose 36-character pattern is replaced with the strict UUID shape in all nine route files that carried it (account, action, auth, classification, compose, connection-test, message, search, send - the ledger named account-routes only). A 36-character wrong-shape id now rejects with 400 at the boundary. Pre-fix failure: 'expected 404 to be 400' (with a real database the uuid cast turns the same input into a 500).
- Action generation guard: the item loop re-checks the live occurrence's uidvalidity against both the frozen target and the folder row before any write, conflicting as generation_changed. Test moves an occurrence to a new generation after the freeze. Pre-fix failure: the item confirmed and wrote (status confirmed, executor called, revision bumped).
- Bootstrap grant race: issueGrant now takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('auth.grant_issue.<purpose>')) before revoke-and-insert, and re-checks the owner under the lock; issueRecoveryGrant takes the same per-purpose lock. Measured pre-fix shape (15 probe rounds): the enrollment_grants_live_purpose_uidx partial unique index already held the line at one live grant, but every round crashed at least one of four concurrent bootstraps with a raw 'Failed query: insert into enrollment_grants' unique violation - that crash is the defect, not two live grants. Under the lock all four commands answer and one grant stays live. Pre-fix failure: the four-racer Promise.all rejects with the raw insert error.
- Defuddle console.log of extracted content: already absent. grep for console statements across packages/content/src returns nothing; redactDiagnostics already drops removed text. No change made; recorded because the ledger listed it.
Verification: search 36/36, actions 38/38, auth 24/24, api 96/96, content 16/16; tsc --noEmit clean in search, actions, auth, api, content. Residual: a display name that itself contains address-shaped text (an at-sign inside the quoted name) can still surface in from:/to: - the same family T073 tracks for domain:; structured address columns retire it.

tasks.title: Finish deployment and worker polish
tasks.details: The nginx gateway sends no gzip for text assets (deploy/nginx-web.conf.template); add compression with safe defaults. The worker SIGTERM path aborts the cycle controller and stops the queue without awaiting the in-flight cycle transaction. Verify the shutdown waits for the current commit, and surface a rejected queue stop instead of exiting silently. The admin CLI ignores extra arguments after the command, so a typo still runs the intended command; reject unknown arguments. Extend .dockerignore to the e2e fixture outputs so the image context stays small.

tasks.title: Record the F12 device and browser matrix
tasks.details: SPEC F12 requires validation on Safari and macOS and on a real iPhone with an installed PWA, with the tested browser and operating system versions recorded. The browser suites run only the cached Linux Chromium, and no document states which part of the matrix stays untested. Record the covered matrix in the repository, list the untested platforms honestly, and keep the entry point ready for a run on real hardware.

tasks.title: Close the revocation race in authentication ceremonies
tasks.details: consumeChallenge and consumeGrant check only consumedAt is null, never revokedAt (packages/auth/src/state.ts:162 and 204). completeLogin and completeEnrollment read the credential and challenge before their transactions and never re-read revokedAt inside them (packages/auth/src/service.ts:249-276 and 655-687). A ceremony in flight while auth recover or recovery begin commits can still consume the now-revoked challenge and insert a live session or credential afterward, so an owner looping logins with a stolen passkey keeps a working session after the emergency revocation; revokeAllAuthState sets revokedAt on challenges and grants (state.ts:227-259) but nothing reads it on the consumption path. Make consumption require revokedAt is null as well, re-read the credential under the transaction lock before the session or credential insert, and cover the interleaving with a test that revokes all auth state between the ceremony read and its commit.

tasks.title: Fix upload body parsing and the draft clear contract
tasks.details: Two compose-route defects. The upload scope registers only a wildcard buffer parser (apps/api/src/compose-routes.ts:337), but the Fastify built-in text/plain and application/json parsers win over the wildcard, so those two media types arrive as a string and new Uint8Array(string) at line 367 yields zero bytes: the durable store records a zero-byte upload, its hash verifies, and the sent message ships an empty attachment. The web client sends the file's own media type, so .txt and .json attachments trigger it on the normal path. Register buffer parsers for both types in the upload scope, or reject a body that is not a Buffer. Also PATCH /drafts/:id collapses markdown: null into field-absent (compose-routes.ts:268) although the service defines null as clear and subject: null clears, so clearing the draft body silently no-ops.

tasks.title: Chain the offline send path and gate sends on attachments
tasks.details: Three defects in the offline send path. settleSynced chains the base revision only for draft-save payloads (packages/offline/src/sync.ts:542-561), so a queued send keeps the revision frozen at queue time; the send replays against a revision its own preceding edit moved, the server answers draft_stale, and the send lands in manual review. resolveReview's send branch mints a new idempotency key but never advances baseRevision either (sync.ts:316). A draft-save and its send queued in the same millisecond tie on queuedAt, so the send can replay first and mail the pre-edit content; order one draft's save deterministically before its send. And enqueueSend gates only on upload.serverId (sync.ts:394-399): the attach step is never checked and the caller swallows a failed attach (apps/web/src/mail/compose-data.ts:354), so the send can leave without its attachment. Chain sends the way saves chain, break the ordering tie, gate the send on the draft's upload links, and surface the attach failure.
tasks.notes: Fixed 2026-09-20. Four chains closed. settleSynced now chains baseRevision forward for same-draft sends as well as saves, so a queued send replays against the revision its own preceding edit earned instead of landing in review on a false draft_stale. resolveReview's send branch rebases onto the local draft's newest earned revision after minting the fresh idempotency key. pendingActions breaks equal-queuedAt ties by kind rank (upload, then draft-save, then flag and move, then send), so one draft's save always replays before its send. enqueueSend now requires every referenced upload to hold both its server acknowledgement and its attach to the server draft (new attachedAt field, set through markUploadAttached); the queue-send port attaches acknowledged-but-unlinked uploads before POSTing and stops with a retry when an attach fails, and the editor counts refused attaches into the file note instead of swallowing them. Editor wiring: the attachment lists re-read the store at each replay-pass boundary (the queue counters can start and end a pass at the same values, because work queued offline never moved the published snapshot), which also stops a runaway loop: the old truthiness check on the new attach outcome re-triggered a refresh-attach cycle that read the attachment list about 260 times per second. Fail-pre-fix proofs: with records.ts, store.ts, and sync.ts stashed, five offline tests fail (send chaining, tie order, the attach gate, the review rebase, and the orphaned-upload drain); with draft-editor.tsx stashed, the new e2e fails its bounded-polling assertion with 160 attachment-list reads in 600 ms against the allowed 2, and the editor-level attach after a replayed upload is otherwise only covered by that e2e because the Send button already gates on waiting uploads. The queue-level attach-before-send rejection is unit-proven in packages/offline, not e2e-proven: the editor holds its Send button while uploads wait.

tasks.title: Harden the offline replay controller and local store
tasks.details: Five defects in the offline wiring. resolve and retry start a second replay pass while one runs (apps/web/src/offline/sync-context.tsx:106; OfflineSync has no re-entrancy lock), so two concurrent passes double-run port calls and a duplicate draft-save PATCH returns draft_stale that lands a good edit in review. refresh drops a generation change observed mid-pass (sync-context.tsx:60) because it returns while a pass is running, so every pending item then fails the generation check on the next pass instead of a clean stop. refresh has no catch (sync-context.tsx:65), so a Dexie failure becomes an unhandled rejection with a null snapshot. cacheMessageRow and cacheMessageDetail do an unlocked read-modify-write (packages/offline/src/store.ts:86) that can drop the cached detail half. And local draft rows and acknowledged upload rows are never deleted (store.ts:135; deleteLocalDraft has no caller), so Dexie grows without bound. Add a re-entrancy guard, observe a generation change after the pass ends, catch refresh failures, make cache updates atomic, and prune settled local records.
tasks.notes: Fixed 2026-09-20. Re-entrancy: OfflineSync.sync now serializes passes through a private pass promise — a caller that arrives while a pass runs chains behind it and then runs a fresh pass — so resolve and retry can no longer double-run port calls and land a good edit in review on a false draft_stale (the context itself needed no change; its resolve and retry call controller.sync). Mid-pass generation: refresh records the newest generation handed over in a ref and the running pass loops until it consumed it, so a generation that arrives during a pass is observed when the pass can take it instead of being dropped by the early return and replayed item-by-item into recovery_required refusals later. Refresh failures: the pass body sits in a catch, so a Dexie failure keeps the last good snapshot and leaves syncing false instead of an unhandled rejection. Atomic caches: cacheMessageRow and cacheMessageDetail read and write inside one rw transaction, so a row cache and a detail cache that overlap can no longer read the same base record and each drop the other's half. Pruning: pruneSettledLocalRecords runs at the end of every pass and drops non-dirty draft copies and attached uploads older than SETTLED_RECORD_RETENTION_MS (7 days); dirty drafts and unacknowledged or unlinked uploads stay because the review surface and the send gate read them. Fail-pre-fix proofs: with sync.ts stashed, the serialization test fails with a second save:d1 port call while the first hangs in flight; with sync-context.tsx stashed, both new provider tests fail — the generation test observes only the first generation and the failure test records the unhandled rejection; with store.ts stashed, 24 tests fail on the missing prune API, and with only the two cache transactions reverted, the concurrency test fails on the lost half. Context tests render the real provider through createRoot and act over a mocked offlineSync singleton in a new file, apps/web/test/sync-context.test.tsx.

tasks.title: Stop startup recovery from flipping live sends
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. recoverAbandonedAttempts now waits for an attempt lease (ATTEMPT_LEASE_MS, 10 minutes) before it holds a sending or appending row: the selection requires sendingStartedAt or appendStartedAt older than the lease, the append claim stamps the new appendStartedAt column, and the worker repeats the recovery pass every send and Sent-copy cycle instead of only at startup, so a crashed worker's rows resolve without a restart while live submissions keep their claims (packages/send/src/service.ts, apps/worker/src/main.ts). Every sweep (executeQueued, appendDueSentCopies, reconcileUnknownOutcomes) contains per-row failures behind a rowErrors counter, so one poisoned row can no longer abort a pass; its attempt stays claimed until the lease-aged hold picks it up. Starvation is bounded two ways: migration 0007 adds sentCopyAttempts and reconcileAttempts counters, non-stored conclusions and evidence-less passes increment them, a row at SEND_SWEEP_ATTEMPT_CAP (20) leaves the sweep with a send.sent_copy_halted or send.reconcile_halted event, and configuration-blocked rows (a recorded sent_folder_unmapped failure while the account still maps no Sent folder, or an unknown whose account maps none) are excluded from the bounded selection and return the moment a mapping exists. Four regression tests cover the concurrent recovery pass against a live claimed submission, the poisoned row, and both caps; each was verified to fail on the pre-fix code.

tasks.title: Revalidate folder generations inside bulk action loops
tasks.details: executeFolderGroup compares the folder generation once when it selects the group (packages/actions/src/service.ts:404-407) and then performs up to 500 remote writes against frozen UIDs with no recheck. A UIDVALIDITY change during the batch can retarget a later write onto a different message, and a move with no condition can expunge the wrong local occurrence (service.ts:492). The mailbox port already exposes revalidate (packages/actions/src/mailbox.ts:47-48) and sync calls it before every mutation window (packages/sync/src/steady.ts:243), but no actions path calls it. Recheck the generation through the loop, at a bounded interval or before each write, and stop the group as conflicted when the folder moved. This covers the execution window; T061 covers the freeze-time race in the same file.
tasks.notes:
Done. executeFolderGroup now revalidates the selected folder's generation through the item loop, before every item, and stops the group the moment the generation moved: the current item and the rest of the group conflict as generation_changed with the observed generation, keeping the receipts already committed. Per-item was chosen over a bounded interval because the port's revalidate is one SELECT on the open connection and both the write and the no-op confirm read flags fetched against the old generation.
Regression test: two mark_read items in one group; the executor wrapper rebuilds the folder (uidvalidity 1 -> 2) after the first write. Asserts [confirmed, conflicted], outcome reason generation_changed observed 2, one executor call, and the untouched occurrence keeps revision 1. Pre-fix failure (service.ts stashed): 'expected [ confirmed, confirmed ] to deeply equal [ confirmed, conflicted ]' - the second write landed against the rebuilt folder.
T061 (same file) covers the freeze-time race this task left; verification: actions tsc clean, 39/39 tests.

tasks.title: Bound the Jev input window over the whole composed text
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. minimizeMessageInput now cuts the header fields before composing: the collapsed sender is sliced to MAX_SENDER_CHARS (256) and the subject to MAX_SUBJECT_CHARS (512), so the composed text can never exceed MAX_INPUT_CHARS (4096) the way an unbounded folded subject or display name made it (packages/classification/src/input.ts). The truncated flag now reports any cut field, not only the body slice, and the hash still covers the exact text sent. Two regression tests were verified to fail on the pre-fix code (24,608 characters of composed text where 4,096 were assumed). The ESTIMATED_INPUT_TOKENS_PER_CALL cost-cap estimate stays honest because the window it assumes now bounds the real input.

tasks.title: Contain thread-pass failures and prevent parent cycles
tasks.details: The thread pass is the one uncontained step of runAccountCycle: a bare await of reconcileAccount (packages/sync/src/runner.ts:160-178) means a throw skips recordStatus, so the per-account sync.status event never lands and the account shows no cycle at all. A concurrent merge can trigger the throw through the self-foreign-key check in decideLink (packages/sync/src/threads.ts:344) or a deadlock abort, and nothing catches either. Contain the pass the way folders and bodies are contained, and record the status event regardless. Also reconcileRow locks only its own row (threads.ts:223-228) while decideLink reads the parent rows unlocked, so two concurrent passes can commit A.parent_message_id = B and B.parent_message_id = A; the schema forbids only self-parents, both rows clear thread_dirty, and membership stays permanently wrong with nothing that repairs it. Serialize the decision, for example by locking both rows in a stable order or rechecking the pair after commit.
tasks.notes: Fixed 2026-09-20. Containment: runAccountCycle now wraps the thread pass like folders and bodies — a throw increments threadErrors, logs one warn through the runner logger, and the sync.status event still lands; the event payload carries threadErrors and pendingThreads. Serialization: reconcileRow takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('threads.<account>')) as the first statement of its transaction, before any row lock, so every link decision for one account queues behind the previous commit and a later pass reads committed links; the advisory-first order keeps two passes from deadlocking on advisory-plus-row locks. Fail-pre-fix proofs: with runner.ts stashed, the containment test fails because the SyncError escapes runAccountCycle (no status event); with threads.ts stashed, the race test fails with a raw 40P01 deadlock — the two passes block each other on the parent-message foreign-key KEY SHARE while each holds the other row, so the error escapes reconcileAccount uncontained; the same missing serialization is what lets both directions commit and form the A<->B parent cycle the schema cannot see (only self-parents are forbidden). Race test makes the interleave deterministic: A resolves alone first (own thread, no parent), B imports and is the only dirty row, a trigger stalls exactly the write that sets B.parent=A for 2 s, A is re-dirtied mid-flight, and a second pass (A first on newer sentAt) decides against B's uncommitted link. Post-fix the second pass waits on the advisory lock, then flags A ambiguous on the committed B->A link; exactly one direction links and both rows settle. Note: same-order batches are already safe on the row locks; the defect needs divergent batch order between concurrent passes, which sentAt ties make realistic (the fixture Date header ties, so batch order is physical order). Full sync suite 72/72, tsc clean in sync and worker.

tasks.title: Handle empty and multi-role folder imports
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. An empty discovery run no longer reaches the insert: the service skips the values() call when the normalized list is empty, so a connection test that reports zero folders imports nothing instead of surfacing the drizzle "values() must be called with at least one value" error as a 500. The route schema keeps accepting an empty array on purpose: an empty run is a coherent no-op, not a client error. A folder whose hints name two roles now keeps exactly one: the assignment loop writes the chosen role back into the in-memory snapshot it reads candidates from, so the second role can no longer claim a row the same pass already filled; the first role in the fixed role order wins and the result reports only the role the row carries. Both regression tests were verified to fail on the pre-fix code (the raw database error, and a result that claimed both inbox and sent for one row whose stored role was only the last write).

tasks.title: Stop domain filters matching spoofed display names
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. The domain operator and the domain chips now read a new addresses_text column that holds addresses only, sender first, instead of the joined display text. ingestion, header import, and the send writer derive it through a new addressesIndexText helper beside the display-text ones, migration 0009 adds the column with its trigram index and backfills it from the stored jsonb sender and recipients, and the search harness seeds it the same way the writers do. Repairing the match exposed a second defect the old code hid: the mid-list LIKE pattern ended in a bare space, and PostgreSQL LIKE anchors the whole pattern, so it could never match the trimmed text; only the sender and the last recipient ever matched a domain. The patterns are now a suffix for the final address and an address followed by the space of the next one, over the address-only text.
