The regression test seeds a spoof whose display names carry a plain bank.example address and a fullwidth at-sign folded by NFKC, a real sender at the domain, and a middle recipient at the domain followed by another address: the filter returns the last two and never the spoof. Verified to fail on the pre-fix code (the middle recipient was missed); the spoof half guards the new pattern against matching display names, which the old code excluded only by the accident of name-first ordering.

tasks.title: Fix the compose surface state defects
tasks.details: Done 2026-09-20. The reply shortcut now sends the selected row's accountId with the request, so a reply to mail in a later account asks the server about the account that holds the parent; the identity step that follows lists that account's identities instead of accounts[0]'s. Where a reply request still names no account, the screen no longer guesses: an identity_choice_required without accountId shows the account step, and the repeat that names an account gets the true identity list. The editor's dispose path now retires the autosaver with a flush: an edit inside the two-second debounce window, or one parked on a save error, is saved when the editor closes or switches drafts; a conflict stays excluded because nothing saves over it without the explicit choice, and discarding a draft disposes without flushing since its row is gone. In-flight creation no longer outranks navigation: an open draft renders ahead of the creating spinner, every navigation takes a monotonically increasing number so a creation resolving afterwards reloads the list but cannot overwrite the draft the user opened or surface its error, and the draft and list intents clear a visible choice step and a stale createError. New component tests cover the screen (three of four fail on the pre-fix code) and the editor dispose path (both fail on the pre-fix code); the reply e2e now expects the identity step directly because the row names its account, and all 42 flows pass.

tasks.title: Fix the reader, list, and settings interface defects
tasks.details: Five interface defects. A plain-text message leaves the live region announcing the inline-image load forever (apps/web/src/components/mail/reader-pane.tsx:448). After Load images, an http: URL counts as loaded although the frame CSP allows https: only, so the image vanishes with no explanation (apps/web/src/mail/render.ts:165 with markdown.ts:119). A cid: reference that arrives with angle brackets never resolves its part (render.ts:74). Two rapid saves of one settings key can apply out of order, and the late pickPatched repaints the older value over the newer edit (apps/web/src/settings/settings-context.tsx:153); the queued-save fix in T052 protects only different keys. And a manual refresh with more than one fetched page reloads only the last page (apps/web/src/mail/data.ts:540), so serverReadId never rises and the pending overlays never retire; this is the paged counterpart of the single-page defect under T058.

tasks.title: Copy the missing workspace manifests into the image
tasks.details: The npm ci layers of both stages run while packages/classification, packages/content, and packages/settings are absent from the image (Dockerfile:26-41 and 65-80), although apps/worker and apps/api import classification and settings, and packages/reading and packages/compose import content. npm 11 tolerates the missing targets by leaving dangling @mail-hub/* symlinks that the later package COPY restores, so the build works by accident; the arrangement contradicts the file's own comment that every workspace manifest must be present before npm ci, and an npm release that fails on lockfile targets with no directory breaks both stages. Add the three COPY lines to both stages.

tasks.title: Watch disk space and collect unreferenced objects
tasks.details: Two spec-level operations gaps. SPEC section 10 requires monitoring free disk space and pausing imports and uploads before durable writes become unsafe; nothing measures free space, so a full disk surfaces only as per-object write failures, and the short-write assert from T048 catches corruption but nothing pauses the pipeline. And SPEC section 8 requires garbage collection that removes only unreferenced durable objects after a grace period longer than the backup window; nothing implements it, so originals stranded by logical-message merges and uploads left by discarded drafts accumulate forever (packages/ingestion/src/service.ts:444-445 notes the stranded duplicates). Add a free-space check that pauses body fetches and uploads under a threshold with an honest event, and a sweep that deletes only objects no table references, behind the collection pause hook the backup script already defines (T053).

tasks.title: Make the offline send replay converge when the server already holds the attachment link
tasks.details:
A queued offline send can wait forever when its attachment link already exists on the server. queueSend re-posts the attach for any upload whose attachedAt is null (apps/web/src/offline/port.ts:151). When the first attach response was lost after the server committed the draft_uploads row, every later pass repeats the attach, the server answers 500, and classifyReplayFailure maps that 500 to retryable. The send POST never runs, the message shows 'waiting on this device' indefinitely, and enqueueSend refuses new attempts with UploadsUnverifiedError for the same upload. Fix: before attaching, re-list the server draft's attachments (GET /drafts/:id/uploads) and treat any upload the server already references as attached (call markUploadAttached and continue). Coordinate with the server-side idempotency fix (T079) and the reconciliation fix (T080).

Fixed 2026-09-20. queueSend now reads GET /drafts/:id/uploads before the first attach it would repeat (lazily, once per replay) and calls store.markUploadAttached for any upload the server already references, so a lost first attach response converges on the next pass instead of re-POSTing into the committed draft_uploads row forever. A failed list read classifies through classifyReplayFailure like every other replay request.

tasks.title: Make draft upload attachment idempotent on the server
tasks.details:
attachUpload inserts into draft_uploads without checking for an existing row, so a repeated attach violates the (draftId, uploadId) primary key and the API answers an unclassified 500 internal_error (packages/compose/src/service.ts:487). An offline replay that lost its first attach response hits this on every pass, which wedges the queued send (see T078). Fix: inside the transaction, select the existing draft_uploads row for (draftId, uploadId) first and return it as the attachment record, so a retry after a lost response converges instead of failing.

Fixed 2026-09-20. attachUpload selects the existing draft_uploads row through a new findDraftUpload helper inside the transaction and returns it unchanged, so a retry after a lost response converges instead of violating the primary key with an unclassified 500. The idempotent path records no second event and skips the aggregate byte check, whose re-run would double-count the recorded row.

tasks.title: Mark server-attached uploads as attached during draft reconciliation
tasks.details:
attachAcknowledgedUploads skips uploads the server draft already references without calling store.markUploadAttached, so a local record left at serverId-set and attachedAt-null never converges (apps/web/src/mail/compose-data.ts:352). Offline sends of that draft then reject with UploadsUnverifiedError permanently, and the stuck record is invisible because localUploadsOf lists only rows with serverId null. Fix: when the server references the upload, call markUploadAttached before continuing.

Fixed 2026-09-20. attachAcknowledgedUploads calls store.markUploadAttached for uploads the server attachment list already references, so a record left at serverId-set/attachedAt-null converges and OfflineSync.enqueueSend accepts the draft's send again.

tasks.title: Block the send when the autosaver ends in the error or offline state
tasks.details:
submitSend blocks a send only when the autosaver ends in state 'conflict' (apps/web/src/components/mail/draft-editor.tsx:426). When the flush ends in state 'error' (the PATCH failed with a non-network error, or the offline queue write failed), the code proceeds to requestDraftSend with the last saved revision. The server freezes that stale snapshot and locks the draft, so the pending edits in autosaver memory can never be saved and the mail goes out without them. Fix: after the awaited flush, gate the send on autosaver.pendingPatch === null (or state 'saved'), show a note for the 'error' and 'offline' states that matches the conflict gate, and gate canSend the same way.

Fixed 2026-09-20. submitSend gates on autosaver.pendingPatch after the awaited flush, not only on the conflict state, with matching notes for the error and offline states; canSend blocks those states too, and the uncertain panel's send-again path now shares the gate.

tasks.title: Map IngestionError to its documented status in the message routes
tasks.details:
The scoped handler in apps/api/src/message-routes.ts:48 classifies only ReadingError and AuthError, so IngestionError from attachment regeneration and sanitized-body refresh surfaces as a generic 500 internal_error. The per-code status table in packages/ingestion/src/errors.ts (unsupported_locator 422, not_found 404, and so on) says it exists so the download routes report the same way, but no route consumes it. Fix: add an IngestionError branch that replies with error.httpStatus and the error code and message, mirroring the ReadingError branch.

Fixed 2026-09-20. The scoped message-route handler gained an IngestionError branch mirroring the ReadingError branch, replying with error.httpStatus and the code and message, so regeneration failures keep the statuses packages/ingestion/src/errors.ts documents instead of surfacing as generic 500 internal_error.

tasks.title: Handle SIGTERM that arrives during worker startup
tasks.details:
A SIGTERM that arrives during worker startup, after waitForReadyService resolves but before setup completes, never triggers the graceful stop (apps/worker/src/main.ts:83). queue.start(), the durable-object collection pass, the four queue work registrations, and the four armSchedule calls do not observe the abort signal, and only the sync-cycle handler checks shutdown.signal.aborted. The process then lingers with live schedules until SIGKILL, which can kill a cycle mid-transaction. Fix: register one signal handler at the top of main() that aborts the controller and runs stopWorker once the queue and pool exist, or check the abort signal after setup completes and run the stop sequence then.

Fixed 2026-09-20. One exported installWorkerSignals helper installs a single SIGINT/SIGTERM listener at the top of main(); before the queue exists a signal only aborts, and armStop installs the stop gate at the end of setup, running the graceful stop itself when the signal already aborted so main returns instead of running cycles on a process asked to stop. The pre-existing once-pair fell through to the default kill on a second signal; the new listener serves the whole lifetime.

tasks.title: Apply one case rule to the reserved INBOX name in folder import
tasks.details:
rolesOf grants the inbox role for any case-insensitive 'inbox' spelling, but folder identity is exact-case: the byName map, the discovery deduplication, and the folders unique key all compare case-sensitively (packages/accounts/src/service.ts:353, packages/accounts/src/validation.ts:202). A discovery run that reports 'Inbox' after 'INBOX' inserts a second folder row for the same mailbox (RFC 3501 permits the spelling change), reports a spurious role conflict, and the duplicate row is permanent because no API deletes folders. Verified by reproduction on a real PostgreSQL. Fix: canonicalize any case-insensitive inbox spelling onto one stored name, or apply one case rule to rolesOf, normalizeDiscoveredFolders, and the byName lookup.

Fixed 2026-09-20. One exported case rule folderKey(name) keys the reserved inbox name case-insensitively and every other name exactly; normalizeDiscoveredFolders deduplicates on it (two spellings in one run reject as a duplicate) and importFolders remaps a re-spelled inbox onto the stored row, so the second run inserts nothing and reports no conflict. Regression test imports INBOX then Inbox against PostgreSQL.

tasks.title: Make sender override identity case-insensitive and the read deterministic
tasks.details:
CorrectionService writes sender overrides with the raw wire-case address and keys the upsert on exact text, so two case variants of one address create two rows. loadSenderOverride reads with lower(sender) = lower(address), limit(1), and no order by, so PostgreSQL returns an unspecified row and an older override can shadow the owner's newest correction for new mail (packages/classification/src/service.ts:450). Fix: normalize the stored sender to lowercase (or replace the primary key with a unique index on (account_id, lower(sender))), and order the read so the newest override wins.

Fixed 2026-09-20. CorrectionService stores the sender override keyed lowercase, so two case variants of one address upsert one row; loadSenderOverride orders the lookup with the lowercase-canonical row first and a stable sender tiebreak, so the read is deterministic. The row carries no timestamp, so newest-wins is derived structurally: the canonical row is the only one the fixed upsert maintains. CorrectionResult.sender and the class.corrected payload keep the raw wire-case address.

tasks.title: Re-mark thread jobs whose stored reference text differs from the extracted identifier
tasks.details:
markThreadJobsDirty re-marks children with exact equality on in_reply_to, but resolveParentReference extracts identifiers from the raw stored text and tolerates folded comments such as '<(note) <a@example.com>>' (packages/ingestion/src/thread-jobs.ts:71). A child stored with a folded In-Reply-To and empty reference_ids is never re-marked when its parent's holder set changes, so its pending or ambiguous link is permanent because reconcileAccount resolves only dirty rows. Fix: mark rows whose raw in_reply_to or reference_ids contain one of the identifiers, as extraction does, or normalize the stored reference columns to their extracted identifiers at import and parse time.

Fixed 2026-09-20. markThreadJobsDirty keeps its two index-backed exact arms and adds two containment arms in the same UPDATE: in_reply_to LIKE ANY over the escaped identifiers, and a correlated EXISTS over jsonb_array_elements_text(reference_ids) with the same match — the shape extraction itself uses for folded comments. LIKE wildcards inside an identifier are escaped, and a database-backed suite proves the folded child flips dirty both through direct marking and the real ingestOriginal path.

tasks.title: Clear the draft dirty flag when a queued send finishes its replay
tasks.details:
moreEditsPending counts any pending action for the draft, including a queued send, so the local draft keeps its dirty flag after an offline replay finishes (packages/offline/src/sync.ts:604). snapshot.dirtyDrafts stays at 1 forever, which contradicts the records contract ('true while the local edits have no server acknowledgement'), the Dexie record is never pruned, and a later server restore leaves reviewRequired permanently true with no reviewable item. Fix: count only queued draft-saves as unsynchronized edits, and clear the dirty flag in settleSynced when a send of that draft syncs.

Fixed 2026-09-20. settleSynced counts only queued draft-saves as unsynchronized edits (hasQueuedDraftSave), and a new send branch clears the local draft's dirty flag — and restamps its recovery generation — when a send of that draft syncs and its base revision covers the local base, because the send's revision gate proves the server holds those edits. dirtyDrafts reaches 0, the Dexie record prunes after retention, and a restored generation no longer leaves reviewRequired permanently true.

tasks.title: Fall back to the stored sanitized body when a refresh fails
tasks.details:
currentSanitizedHtml awaits refreshSanitizedBody with no failure handling; the null fallback covers only a null return (packages/reading/src/service.ts:205). When the refresh throws (original missing, hash mismatch, or parse failure after a sanitizer version bump or a partial restore), GET /messages/:id and /clean-view answer a generic 500, so the user loses subject, recipients, and attachments too, even though only htmlSanitized depends on the refresh. Fix: catch refresh failures and fall back to the stored sanitized derivative, or serve every non-HTML field from the row and log the failure server-side.

Fixed 2026-09-20. currentSanitizedHtml catches refresh failures, logs one console.warn with the message id and cause, and returns the stored sanitized derivative — prior sanitizer output, never the original — so GET /messages/:id and /clean-view serve every field instead of a 500.

tasks.title: Record the sent event only when the acceptance status transition commits
tasks.details:
commitAcceptance records the sent event and inserts the local sent message even when its status-guard update matched no row (packages/send/src/service.ts:1270). When the SMTP submission outlives its lease and the row moved to outcome_unknown, the acceptance transaction commits while the outbound row stays unresolved and the draft stays locked, and the row can never auto-resolve because the Sent-copy path requires status 'sent'. Fix: mirror concludeSentCopy. When the guarded update matches no row, roll back without recording the event and without keeping the inserted message.

Fixed 2026-09-20. commitAcceptance commits the sent event, the local message, and the draft unlock only when its status-guard update matches a row; otherwise a private AcceptanceSupersededError rolls the transaction back and the caller receives the re-read row, keeping the outcome_unknown evidence path open.

tasks.title: Remove or implement the hardcoded /health route
tasks.details:
GET /health returns a constant 'ok' response and checks nothing, while /healthz does the real database round trip and answers 503 on failure (apps/api/src/app.ts:32). Nothing consumes /health: the SPEC, the Dockerfile healthcheck, and deploy/README.md all use /healthz only. An operator or monitor that probes the conventional /health path sees 'ok' during a full outage. Fix: delete the route, or implement it over HealthService.readHealth so it cannot answer ok while the database is down.

Fixed 2026-09-20. Deleted the constant GET /health route and the unused contracts import in app.ts; the test now pins the 404. /healthz remains the real check. Follow-up: the HealthResponse interface in packages/contracts/src/index.ts is now orphaned but was left in place because contracts sat inside another session's active edits.

tasks.title: Keep the drafts sidebar content visible during a refresh
tasks.details:
Every reloadDrafts call drives use-resource through its nonce dependency, which resets data to null, so the drafts sidebar unmounts its list and shows a spinner until the refetch answers (apps/web/src/components/mail/compose-screen.tsx:236). This contradicts the keep-content-visible refresh rule the useResource doc comment states (SPEC F12). Fix: keep the last ready data visible while a reload is in flight, and use the spinner as an overlay rather than a replacement.

Fixed 2026-09-20. useResource tracks the inputs of the last run: a rerun over the same inputs (a reload) keeps the last ready answer in data while loading, while changed inputs still reset to a blank slate so one message's answer never shows under another's load. The drafts sidebar keeps its list mounted with the spinner overlaying it.

tasks.title: Surface controller errors in review and failed-action rows
tasks.details:
Review and failed-action rows call resolve, retry, discard, compare, and keepServerCopy with no rejection handling (apps/web/src/components/mail/sync-status.tsx:305). resolveReview deliberately throws ReviewChoiceError when the queued action no longer exists (for example a second tab resolved it first), so the promise rejects unhandled and the row sits with no explanation. Fix: catch rejections in run, compare, and keepServerCopy, show the error text in the row, and keep the busy state consistent.

Fixed 2026-09-20. FailedItemRow and ReviewItemRow run every step through one guarded run(): resolve, retry, discard, compare, and keepServerCopy each catch and show the error's own words in the row (a helper keeps ApiError and ReviewChoiceError messages), and the busy flag settles in finally; a failed adoption no longer discards the item.

tasks.title: Keep the acknowledged upload id when the attach step fails
tasks.details:
When the server acknowledges an upload but the attach step then fails with a non-network refusal, addFileToDraft returns 'rejected' and discards the acknowledged upload id (apps/web/src/mail/compose-data.ts:230). Nothing on the device records it, so the link can never be retried, the owner must upload the same bytes again, and the first upload becomes an unreferenced object. Fix: on a non-network attach failure, persist the acknowledged upload into the offline store with serverId set and attachedAt null, as queueUpload does, so the next pass retries the link.

Fixed 2026-09-20. addFileToDraft separates the byte upload from the attach; when the upload is acknowledged but the attach is refused with a non-network error, rememberAcknowledgedUpload persists the upload into the offline queue with serverId set, attachedAt null, and empty bytes, so the next pass retries only the link. Network attach failures keep the existing re-queue-with-bytes behavior.

tasks.title: Degrade the folder index per account instead of failing every account
tasks.details:
useFolderIndex fetches every account's folders with Promise.all, so one transient failure on one account rejects the whole read and the nav pane and unified inbox error everywhere (apps/web/src/mail/data.ts:300). The merge guard 'if (response !== undefined)' is dead code, which shows partial tolerance was intended but never implemented. Fix: use Promise.allSettled, build the index from the fulfilled responses, and surface the rejected accounts separately.

Fixed 2026-09-20. useFolderIndex settles every account's read with Promise.allSettled, builds the index from the fulfilled responses, and collects rejected account ids in a new failedAccounts field on FolderIndex; only a total failure rethrows so the existing whole-index error path renders unchanged. No UI renders failedAccounts yet — a rejected account shows as skeleton rows until a successful reload.

tasks.title: Record unexpected per-account sync failures with detail
tasks.details:
runAccountCycle logs every unexpected failure as the literal 'unexpected failure' with no name, message, or stack, then returns normally, so the queue job completes as success and no events row is written (apps/worker/src/main.ts:490). A connection error or programming bug leaves only a degraded log line and growing sync lag. Fix: log the cause name and message (and the stack for non-SyncError causes), and record one events row such as 'sync.failed' so the failure is visible in the durable audit trail.

Fixed 2026-09-20. runAccountCycle logs the cause name and message (plus the stack for non-SyncError causes) and records one sync.failed events row with actor system and payload {accountId, kind}, modeled on classification's class.error; the insert is .catch-guarded so an audit-write failure cannot fail the queue job.

tasks.title: Return the assigned role in importFolders created entries
tasks.details:
importFolders builds the created list from the INSERT ... returning() snapshot, captured before the role-assignment loop runs, so a folder the same import just role-assigned still reports role null in created while assignedRoles and folders report the role (packages/accounts/src/service.ts:401). Fix: build created from the final read inside the transaction, or document and serialize created as names only.

Fixed 2026-09-20. created now filters the final folder read inside the transaction by the ids the INSERT returned, so a folder the same import role-assigned reports its role in created, matching assignedRoles and folders.

tasks.title: Reject control characters in identity display names
tasks.details:
normalizeIdentityName trims and length-checks the display name but never applies CONTROL_PATTERN, unlike normalizeUsername and normalizeFolderName in the same file (packages/accounts/src/validation.ts:162). A stored name with a C0 control character is sealed into the outbound From header as a Q-encoded =00 or =1B inside an encoded-word, which strict receiving MTAs reject or mangle at delivery time. Fix: apply CONTROL_PATTERN to the trimmed name and throw invalid_request, and add the same pattern to the identity schema in the route so the browser gets a 400.

Fixed 2026-09-20. normalizeIdentityName applies CONTROL_PATTERN and throws invalid_request like the sibling normalizers, and the identity schema in account-routes gained an anchored no-control pattern so the route rejects with 400 before the service runs.

tasks.title: Reject local parts with leading, trailing, or consecutive dots
tasks.details:
EMAIL_PATTERN puts the dot in the general local-part class with no structural rule, so '..@example.com', 'a..b@example.com', and '.foo@example.com' all pass and are stored (packages/accounts/src/validation.ts:34). RFC 5321 dot-atom syntax forbids leading, trailing, and consecutive dots, and SMTP servers enforce it, so the failure surfaces only at submission time as an opaque outbound error. Fix: require dot-atom structure for the local part.

Fixed 2026-09-20. EMAIL_PATTERN requires RFC 5321 dot-atom structure for the local part (atoms of the existing class separated by single dots, 64-character ceiling via lookahead), so leading, trailing, and consecutive dots reject while the previously accepted atom characters still pass.

tasks.title: Re-validate the WebAuthn counter under the ceremony transaction lock
tasks.details:
Assertion counters are validated against a pre-transaction snapshot and never re-checked under the FOR UPDATE lock inside the ceremony transaction (packages/auth/src/service.ts:270). Concurrent ceremonies from a cloned passkey can both pass clone detection, and the unconditional write can regress the stored counter. Fix: inside the transaction, select the credential row for update, reject when the new counter is not greater than the stored one (except for counterless authenticators), and persist the counter only through that guarded update.

Fixed 2026-09-20. requireLiveCredential selects the counter in its FOR UPDATE read and rejects with webauthn_invalid when (newCounter > 0 || row.counter > 0) && newCounter <= row.counter — the library's own rule re-applied under the lock — with both zero passing for counterless authenticators. The counter persists only through the guarded update in the same transaction, so concurrent ceremonies from a cloned passkey serialize and the loser is rejected.

tasks.title: Cap the derived reply quote inside the Markdown ceiling
tasks.details:
capDerivedQuote can return up to MARKDOWN_MAX + 6 characters, which violates the ceiling its doc comment promises (packages/compose/src/service.ts:842). The reply draft stores because the column is unlimited, but every later PATCH that sends the Markdown back is rejected with 400 by the route schema and normalizeMarkdown. The trigger needs a parent whose extracted quote exceeds 1,000,000 characters. Fix: slice the kept portion to MARKDOWN_MAX minus the marker length before the last-newline search, so the result always fits.

Fixed 2026-09-20. capDerivedQuote reserves the marker length below the ceiling (QUOTE_MARKER constant) before the last-newline search, so the joined result is at most MARKDOWN_MAX and a later PATCH returning the stored Markdown verbatim passes the length check.

tasks.title: Serve attachment metadata from the row the regenerated bytes verified against
tasks.details:
openAttachment builds the served view from one row snapshot but, on a cache miss, serves bytes that regenerateAttachment verified against a later read of the same row (packages/reading/src/service.ts:233). A concurrent re-ingestion commit between the two reads can pair the old filename and media type with the new bytes, because upsertAttachments reuses the attachment id for the same partPath. Fix: have the regenerator return the row it verified against and serve that row's view, or re-read the one attachment row after regeneration.

Fixed 2026-09-20. AttachmentRegenerator returns the row the regenerated bytes verified against, and openAttachment serves that row's filename and content type overlaid on the snapshot view, so a concurrent re-ingestion can no longer pair old metadata with new bytes. No ingestion or API change was needed: regenerateAttachment already returned the updated row and the wiring satisfies the widened type structurally.

tasks.title: Gate saved-search writes before input validation
tasks.details:
createSavedSearch parses name, query, and scope before the recovery gate, so a stale-generation client that submits an unparseable query gets 400 invalid_query instead of 409 recovery_required, which delays the resync path (packages/search/src/service.ts:411). Every other mutation service gates first. Fix: move gateMutation to the first statement of createSavedSearch and deleteSavedSearch.

Fixed 2026-09-20. gateMutation is the first statement of createSavedSearch and deleteSavedSearch, matching every other mutation service; a stale generation now answers 409 recovery_required before malformed input is parsed, with the doc comments stating the order.

tasks.title: Stop the Sent-copy sweep from starving on unmapped unknown rows
tasks.details:
appendDueSentCopies selects unknown-status rows in accounts that map no Sent folder, but executeSentCopyAppend returns early with attempted false for them, so sentCopyAttempts never increments and the row never reaches the cap or leaves the limit-bounded window (packages/send/src/service.ts:709). With enough such rows, younger due rows are never reached. The method doc states the opposite invariant. Fix: exclude every non-pending row whose account maps no Sent folder, or count the early pass toward the cap so the row records the halt event.

Fixed 2026-09-20. appendDueSentCopies excludes every non-pending row whose account maps no Sent folder — composed like the reconcile sweep's not(missingSentFolder()) — while pending rows stay due for their single pass that records the unmapped failure. A backdated-rows test proves a one-row window goes to the younger row and a fresh Sent mapping re-dues the stuck row.

tasks.title: Remove private data from sync diagnostics
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/sync-repair-plan.md (section T104).

The sync runner logs arbitrary error messages and folder names. Database errors can include private mail parameters. Replace raw errors with approved codes and internal identifiers. Test nested causes and arbitrary thrown values with sentinel secrets. Preserve containment and durable error counters.
steps: Follow the T104 procedure and acceptance checks in docs/sync-repair-plan.md.
Add the required regression coverage and record validation results.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-20. New packages/sync/src/diagnostics.ts classifies every contained failure into an approved kind (sync/storage/ingestion codes, database_<sqlstate>, system_<errno>, error_<name>, unknown); the SQLSTATE branch requires a digit so five-letter errnos (EPIPE, EPERM) stay system_*. runner.ts logs folder/body/thread containment with internal ids and the kind only, and adds deduplicated, bounded *FailureKinds arrays to the summary and sync.status payload. Worker main.ts logs classifyFailure kinds for the outer cycle, temp sweep, and durable collection; the full-volume pause emits fixed text and {kind, code}; the pause, sweep, and collection handlers are now exported and tested. compose upload-pause event aligned to {kind, code}. Verification: diagnostics 22, steady 28 (storage_* through the real runner; dedup and 8-kind bound), worker 21; fail-pre-fix proofs for the classifier and mutation proofs for every new log/payload pin; npm run check clean; full suite 99 files / 1067 tests / 0 failed. Plan step 6 (live worker-log review) blocked: awc-pilot SSH unreachable; folds into T107/T110.

tasks.title: Handle NUL characters in imported mail data
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/sync-repair-plan.md (section T105).

Trash and Deleted Messages repeatedly fail message inserts with PostgreSQL UTF8 error 0x00. The exact field remains unknown. Reproduce with synthetic data and make derived text and nested metadata database-safe. Preserve invalid identifier and address semantics, original bytes, hashes, and atomic checkpoints. Test real PostgreSQL imports, retries, and body ingestion without duplicates or skipped mail.
steps: Follow the T105 procedure and acceptance checks in docs/sync-repair-plan.md.
Add the required regression coverage and record validation results.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-20. Policy: replaceNul/replaceNulOption in packages/ingestion/src/text.ts replace U+0000 with U+FFFD at the derived-data boundary, applied identically in header import (packages/sync/src/headers.ts) and full parse (packages/ingestion/src/parse.ts), so a message looks identical before and after its body fetch and thread linking still matches by string equality. tasks.title: Report partial sync failures in health and settings
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/sync-repair-plan.md (section T106).

The health report shows ok while two folders repeatedly fail. Expose durable per-cycle error counters and safe failure state through health, sync status, and account settings. Distinguish normal backfill from partial failure and stale cycles. A clean cycle clears degradation. Preserve query bounds, privacy, and HTTP liveness behavior.
steps: Follow the T106 procedure and acceptance checks in docs/sync-repair-plan.md.
Add the required regression coverage and record validation results.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. Derivation: HealthService derives one HealthzSyncState per account from its newest sync.status event (packages/observability/src/health.ts): degraded when folderErrors+bodyErrors+threadErrors > 0 however recent the cycle is, stale when clean but older than SYNC_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS = 900 s (exported), syncing when clean and fresh with pending backfill, bodies, or threads (pending work is never a failure), ok when clean, current, and idle, unknown when no record exists or the record predates the T104 counters (missing fields prove nothing). Precedence: errors before stale before pending. Pure computation over the existing distinct-on sync.status query: no SQL added, the read stays read-only and bounded at the same query count. Whole report status: degraded when recovery is not ready OR any account state is degraded; stale and unknown stay per-account only (a fresh enrollment is unknown; stale can follow an operator cron override). /healthz still answers 200 while degraded, so container liveness never restarts on mail trouble. Contracts: HealthzSyncLag gained state, folderErrors/bodyErrors/threadErrors (number|null), folderFailureKinds/bodyFailureKinds/threadFailureKinds (string[]|null), pendingThreads (number|null). The public /healthz response schema was widened to match (Fastify serialization would otherwise silently strip the fields); a route test pins the passthrough with 200 while degraded. /sync/status serves the same accounts unchanged. Web: AccountSyncLines renders one state line (Sync in progress; Sync failed for N folders, M bodies, K threads with the approved codes; No sync cycle recently; Sync up to date; No sync cycle yet; Sync state unknown) beside the existing progress lines; the settings e2e pins a syncing account beside a degraded one. Privacy: every response carries counts and approved kind codes only; no folder names, mail text, or error text in any public or session-gated response. Coverage: packages/observability/test/health.test.ts adds failed-cycle-beside-healthy (the healthy sibling is asserted), clear-after-clean-cycle, stale-beyond-bound without failing the report, pre-T104 record and never-cycled account read unknown, and pending bodies alone stay syncing with the report ok. apps/api tests pin the /healthz passthrough and the /sync/status state fields. Verification: npm run check clean; full suite 99 files / 1080 tests / 0 failed (4 new); e2e flows and settings a11y pass. Review: a 9-agent adversarial workflow (3 dimensions, per-finding refutation) confirmed one coverage gap, fixed pre-commit: the healthy sibling assertion. Mutation proof: forcing every account degraded when any account fails passed 9/9 before the fix and fails three tests after it. Five findings refuted. One valid follow-up observation recorded: whole-cycle sync.failed events are not consulted, so an account failing before recordStatus keeps state ok for up to 900 s and stale after; that is out of T106 scope by plan step 1 and the no-new-queries bound, and it is no regression against HEAD - a future task could surface sync.failed and storage pauses in health.

tasks.title: Verify external API contracts with synthetic requests
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t108-verify-external-api-contracts-with-synthetic-requests

The original tests accepted an incorrect TypeSafe endpoint and response shape. The adapter is fixed; this task prevents recurrence.

Acceptance: A deliberately incorrect endpoint or response fixture fails offline checks. An authorized synthetic live check verifies the configured service without real mail, secret output, or database mutations.
steps: Keep offline contract fixtures traceable to official documentation and a reviewed model version. Cover endpoint, authentication, request shape, typed answers, and error responses.
Add an explicit synthetic smoke command that calls the adapter with invented text. Resolve the API key from the runtime environment and print only approved result fields.
Set request timeouts and a small call budget. Keep live requests out of default tests and untrusted pull requests. Missing credentials produce an explicit unverified result.
Run the smoke check when the adapter, question set, model, or endpoint changes. Verify the installed adapter after deployment.

tasks.title: Expand synthetic malformed-mail regression coverage
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t109-expand-synthetic-malformed-mail-regression-coverage

The NUL-byte incident showed that clean fixtures omit important incoming-mail cases. T105 owns the incident fix and its essential regression tests.

Acceptance: The corpus detects the known NUL regression and unsafe normalization of addresses or identifiers. Tests prove that adjacent valid mail progresses without silent message loss.
steps: Extend the shared synthetic corpus with raw and decoded NUL characters, missing or malformed headers, folded references, nested address metadata, and attachment metadata.
Exercise header import, complete-message ingestion, search derivatives, and thread reconciliation through their real boundaries. Use PostgreSQL for database representation cases.
Check valid Unicode, original and attachment hashes, retry idempotency, and checkpoint atomicity. Assert that each malformed case either imports safely or reports a contained failure.
Document how to reduce a future incident into a synthetic fixture. Never commit raw provider mail or extract private log parameters as fixtures.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. Corpus: packages/harness/src/malformed.ts owns the malformed bytes as builders returning fresh {headers, body} strings (12 builders plus ATTACHMENT_EDGE_PARTS); malformedMailBytes joins them exactly as FakeMessage.completeBytes does, so the fake mailbox, the parser, and the wire all see one byte shape. NUL is spelled String.fromCharCode(0) so no source file carries a control byte; every value is deterministic. Covers raw and decoded NUL (subject, Message-ID, References, quoted-printable body and filename, base64 body), per-field missing headers, garbage header lines, folded References/In-Reply-To, RFC 2822 address groups with encoded-word names, RFC 2231 extended and continued filenames, a nameless part, a zero-byte part, inline parts, and two valid neighbors (one full of non-ASCII). Self-tests (packages/harness/test/malformed.test.ts, 8 tests) pin determinism, the byte round trip, NUL presence exactly where claimed and absence everywhere else (derived from the whole corpus, not a hand list), missing-header exactness, folding and 2231 shapes, parse-without-throw, and no private facts (example.com/example.net only). Real defect found by the corpus: toEmailAddresses in packages/ingestion/src/text.ts dropped RFC 2822 group members silently (mailparser nests them under `group`); it now flattens them in place, keeping valid addresses in order; packages/send/src/view.ts maps stored Recipients rows only, so it inherits the fix upstream. Teeth proven by reverting each fix: replaceNul revert fails 2 header + 4 parse + 3 backfill tests; group-flatten revert fails 1+1+1; a NUL planted in a NUL-free fixture fails the corpus self-test. sync and ingestion dev-depend on @mail-hub/harness for the corpus. docs/sync-repair-plan.md documents how to reduce an incident into a fixture (smallest byte shape, example domains and invented local parts only, deterministic bytes, builder with docblock, register in the self-test, assert at real boundaries, prove teeth); never raw provider mail or private log parameters. Adversarial review (three dimension reviewers plus per-finding refuters): two confirmed findings fixed (the NUL-absence check was a hand-maintained list; it now derives from the corpus; the F2-equivalence it.each rendered four identical titles, now $name-tagged); the refuted attachment-order finding hardened with orderBy(partPath) matching repo convention; three other refutations accepted on the refuters' traces. tasks.title: Document and preflight deployment access
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t110-document-and-preflight-deployment-access

SSH access required host verification and a dedicated authorized key during diagnosis. A local identity path must remain configurable.

Acceptance: A fresh authorized workstation can follow the runbook and confirm required access with one command. Failure output identifies the missing capability without exposing credentials.
steps: Document the application URL, Coolify resource identifier, repository, main branch, compose path, SSH user, and tailnet host in the operator runbook.
Document the dedicated SSH identity override, host-key verification, public-key enrollment, rotation, and revocation. Store no private key or token in the repository.

Add a read-only operator access check, separate from the container environment preflight. Distinguish unavailable tailnet routing, host-key mismatch, denied SSH, and unavailable Docker or Coolify access.
Allow a configured Coolify API token when available. Report missing capabilities clearly; never dump environment variables or generate new credentials silently.
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-09-21. deploy/access-check.mjs (npm run deploy:access): read-only operator access check, separate from the container preflight. Checks identity file, one batch-mode ssh connect, docker over ssh, optional Coolify API (Bearer token on GET /api/v1/teams), optional app health at /api/healthz. tasks.title: Add one command for deployment verification
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t111-add-one-command-for-deployment-verification

Manual health queries, container inspection, and database checks made verification slow. Container health alone missed the stalled folders.

Acceptance: One command can reject a healthy-container deployment with broken sync. It records bounded evidence, states uncertainty, and never reports a fully verified result when required checks were unavailable.
steps: Add a read-only command that resolves the current application containers and deployed revision from the configured resource. Avoid hard-coded container suffixes.
Report deployment state, revision, restarts, recovery readiness, safe sync failures, per-folder checkpoints, body backlog, classification progress, and existing send outcomes.
Support bounded before-and-after sampling. Evaluate progress only when work is pending; an idle mailbox is not a failure. Separate normal backlog from a stalled or failing operation.
Use safe API fields or narrow aggregate database queries. Never print raw logs, addresses, folder names, message content, or secrets. Handle partial access as unverified.
Produce both a machine-readable result and a short report with verified workflows, progressing work, known failures, and untested behavior. Include timestamps and revision.
Test wrong revisions, partial folder failures, clean idle accounts, unavailable containers, missing privileges, and observation timeouts. Do not send or mutate mail to verify a deployment.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. deploy/verify-deployment.mjs (npm run deploy:verify): one read-only command that judges the deployment, not just container health. Three evidence sources, each optional and classified when unavailable: Docker (local, or over SSH via DEPLOY_SSH_HOST with every remote argument single-quoted for the remote shell) for containers, restarts, and revision; the public health endpoint at DEPLOY_APP_URL/api/healthz for recovery, per-account sync, and send counters; and two constant aggregate psql queries through docker exec in the database container (counts only, no folder names or addresses; DEPLOY_DB_CONTAINER/DEPLOY_DB_USER/DEPLOY_DB_NAME override the defaults). Verdicts verified/failed/unverified; exit 0 only when verified; untested areas listed (no --expect-revision, single sample, no accounts). Containers resolve by compose labels, never hard-coded names. A container fails when it is not running, unhealthy, paused, or restart-looping with a fresh start (RestartCount alone never fails an old stable container); a health check still starting keeps the section unverified. --expect-revision accepts a tag, revision label, or sha256 digest (imageId), and an empty value counts as absent. Accounts fail on degraded or stale sync even without pending work; idle accounts never fail. Sampling (--sample-interval 5..300, NaN rejected) judges per account: any counter change in either direction or folder-checkpoint movement is progressing; pending work without movement is stalled; a missing second sample gates the verdict unverified instead of slipping past; a failed second database read downgrades stalled to unknown. A degraded or stale account also fails the health section on a single-sample run. Privacy: output holds states, counts, timestamps, UUIDs, container and image names, and the transport target only. Read-only: no mail is sent or mutated, no credentials are generated, all docker calls are ps/inspect/exec psql SELECT. Unit tests: apps/admin/test/verify-deployment.test.ts (26 tests) pin the acceptance case (pending work without movement between samples reads stalled and fails the verdict) plus parsers and edge inputs. Verified live against a local compose stack of the current tree: idle healthy stack VERIFIED exit 0 (local and over an SSH loopback alias); wrong revision FAILED exit 1; exact sha256 digest VERIFIED; sampled run with no accounts VERIFIED with untested entries; shell-injection payloads in DEPLOY_COMPOSE_PROJECT and DEPLOY_DB_CONTAINER over SSH create no files and read as literal filters (UNVERIFIED exit 1). Adversarial review (3 reviewers + per-finding refuters, 17 findings, 10 confirmed) drove the fixes: ssh remote-shell quoting (injection plus a broken ssh transport), the ungated second sample, stale sync reading idle, growing backlog reading stalled, the failed second database read, the empty revision expectation, the digest mismatch, never-started/paused containers, the lifetime restart count, first-sample degraded accounts, the Coolify database credentials, and npm banner pollution of piped --json output. Full suite: 101 files, 1132 tests, 0 unhandled errors. Runbook: deploy/README.md 'Verify a deployment'.

tasks.title: Isolate browser fixtures for every test run
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t112-isolate-browser-fixtures-for-every-test-run

Local browser tests could reuse a stale server on port 4180. A manually chosen free port worked, but needs automation.

Acceptance: Both concurrent runs test their intended build without shared-server contamination. The unrelated server survives, and failed startup cannot produce a passing result.
steps: Give each browser run its own fixture server, port, and ownership token. Verify a build fingerprint and run identity before tests start.
Handle port allocation races with bounded retries. Preserve E2E_PORT as an explicit override and report collisions clearly.
Prevent concurrent runs from overwriting shared build output. Use an isolated output directory or an explicit build lock.
Terminate only the server owned by the run on success, failure, and interruption. Keep traces for failures.
Verify behavior with a stale unrelated server on 4180 and with two concurrent runs. Keep release checks from silently reusing any existing server.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. Launcher: apps/web/e2e/fixture-launch.mjs gives every run its own fixture — it binds 127.0.0.1 first (503 hold while building), builds with vite --outDir plus build-sw --dist into tmpdir()/mail-hub-e2e-<pid>-<token8>, fingerprints the tree (scripts/build-fingerprint.mjs, sha256 over sorted paths and bytes), then swaps the real fixture handler in behind the bound listener. GET /api/fixture/identity answers {runToken, fingerprint, port}; e2e/fixture-global-setup.ts verifies the token before the first test and the fingerprint at teardown (Playwright 1.63 globalSetup takes a file path, not a closure). E2E_PORT stays an exact override (any value naming no port 1-65535 is rejected); otherwise the config leader allocates an ephemeral port and publishes it through E2E_PORT — every worker reloads the config file, so the port, the E2E_RUN_TOKEN/E2E_RUN_PID pair, and the per-run outputDir test-results/run-<pid>-<token8> all derive from one leader mint. reuseExistingServer stays false and teardown uses gracefulShutdown SIGTERM (the default is a group SIGKILL that skips all cleanup); the launcher registers SIGTERM/SIGINT before any directory or build exists, stops its build children, removes its tree, destroys keep-alive connections, and exits clean in every phase including mid-build and startup failure. e2e/run-isolation.mjs sweeps <prefix><pid>-* directories whose pid is dead — no clock, so a live run keeps its directories however long it runs — for both test-results/run-* and the launcher's tmp trees. fixture-server.mjs became an import-side-effect-free createFixtureHandler factory; static serving answers 404 when a file vanishes or a directory holds no index.html instead of crashing. The release gate needed no change: it runs the workspace scripts, which carry the isolation. Verified: unit 195/195 (27 launcher and isolation tests, three of them subprocess CLI runs: held-port collision leaves no directory and the holder survives, SIGTERM with a live keep-alive socket, SIGTERM mid-build), tsc clean, flows 54/54, interface 20/20, two concurrent suites green on separate ports, builds, and results directories, E2E_PORT=4180 against an unrelated live server fails loudly and the stranger survives, planted dead-pid trees swept on the next run. Adversarial review (5 dimensions, 30 agents, per-finding refuters): 25 findings raised, 14 survived, all fixed above; 11 refutations accepted on the refuters' traces.

tasks.title: Diagnose and document Docker build networking
tasks.details:

Acceptance: The root cause is documented with evidence, or explicitly remains unresolved with a verified workaround. Supported builds resolve dependencies without manual trial and error.

tasks.title: Validate task files automatically
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t114-validate-task-files-automatically

The task file contained metadata that its schema rejected. Optional updated_at and notes definitions were added during planning; automated validation is still missing.

Acceptance: A clean checkout validates the current task list. Each malformed fixture fails with a precise task identifier or field path, while historical notes and planned future files remain supported.
steps: Add a repeatable task-validation command using the repository schema and date-time formats. Declare validator dependencies directly if needed.
Reject duplicate task identifiers, missing dependencies, self-dependencies, dependency cycles, and missing source documents.
Validate plan links and section anchors for planned work. Distinguish intended future implementation files from existing source documents, so planned files are not rejected.
Run the command when task files, schema, or referenced plans change. Add focused fixtures for invalid records, broken plan links, and cycles.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. scripts/validate-tasks.mjs validates to-do.json in one pass: JSON Schema draft 2020-12 through ajv 2020 plus ajv-formats (default strict mode, so a misspelled schema keyword fails at compile), task-graph checks (duplicate ids, missing and self dependencies, a DFS cycle with its path spelled out), Plan: references (the file exists; the anchor is a GitHub slug through github-slugger — an em dash drops and every space becomes one hyphen, so #f1--account-management resolves against the SPEC heading; the (section Tnnn) form checks heading text; sentence punctuation and backticks around the path are stripped), source_files existence, and repository-relative files entries (planned files allowed; empty, absolute, and climbing paths rejected). Wrong-typed shapes report the schema issue instead of throwing. npm run validate:tasks runs the CLI; its report prints to stdout, which the release gate logs as task-files.log (check 1 of 7). 34 tests in apps/admin/test/validate-tasks.test.ts cover the module API, malformed shapes, and the CLI's exit codes and streams. Adversarial review: 13 findings confirmed and fixed, 9 refuted.

tasks.title: Stream release-gate progress and retain logs
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t115-stream-release-gate-progress-and-retain-logs

The gate captures output through spawnSync and prints it only after a step finishes. Long steps appear inactive and complicate diagnosis.

Acceptance: A long-running check shows progress at least every 30 seconds. Failed or skipped checks cannot pass because of output text, and interrupted children do not remain running.
steps: Run each gate step with asynchronous process handling. Stream progress and persist complete stdout and stderr without buffering unbounded output in memory.
Keep the exit code authoritative. Preserve the current test-inventory, skipped-suite, migration, and strict-mode checks.
Show elapsed time and a periodic heartbeat for quiet steps. Implement configurable timeouts and interrupt cleanup for the owned process tree.
Retain failed logs and a concise final summary. Never print environment variables or add commands that echo credentials.
Test slow output, silent steps, nonzero exit after a passing-looking summary, timeout, signal interruption, and large output.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-21. scripts/release-gate.mjs runs each step through the exported runStep: the command spawns detached in its own process group, every output line streams to the console as it arrives, and the raw bytes land in the step's log files while only the vitest summary lines (capped at 10,000) and an optional capped stdout capture stay in memory. A quiet step heartbeats one quiet period after its last output (30 seconds by default), each step times out after 30 minutes unless RELEASE_GATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS says otherwise (0 disables, empty means the default), and a timeout or an interrupt (SIGINT/SIGTERM) tears the whole tree down — SIGTERM first, SIGKILL after the grace period — and the step resolves only once the process group is empty, so no child outlives it. The exit code alone decides the outcome: failure notes name a timeout, an interrupt, a command that never started, or a child killed by an outside signal. An interrupt that lands between steps is carried into the next one, the verdict reads INTERRUPTED with exit 130/143 and kept logs, and the final summary lists every check with the total duration. The module stays import-safe and validates the timeout override before any check runs. 22 tests in apps/admin/test/release-gate.test.ts cover streaming, heartbeat bounds, exit-code precedence, tree teardown and escalation, memory caps, the timeout override, and the CLI's interrupt and refusal exits. Adversarial review: 9 findings confirmed and fixed, 4 refuted.

tasks.title: Gate main before automatic deployment
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t116-gate-main-before-automatic-deployment

Pushes to main now deploy immediately. Checks that start only after that push cannot prevent an unverified deployment.

Acceptance: A failing or outdated pull-request check prevents ordinary integration into main. A verified merge deploys once. Fast local checks remain convenient, while release validation remains complete.
steps: Document a fast local loop: focused regression tests and affected workspace type checks first, then the full required checks before integration. Use a conservative full-run fallback when impact is unclear.
Add a continuous integration workflow for pull requests with a scratch PostgreSQL service, browser dependencies, task validation, and the strict release gate. Cache dependencies using the lockfile.
Require the successful check before merging into main through repository rules supported by this repository. Record any plan or permission restriction as a blocker.
Keep the main-push webhook as the deployment trigger after the verified merge. Do not treat a local hook as the only protection or expose deployment secrets to untrusted code.
Check merge-result coverage and current-branch requirements so an outdated successful check cannot authorize a different final tree. Document explicit emergency bypass handling.
Measure focused-check and full-gate durations before and after the changes. Optimize repeated setup without removing required suites.

tasks.title: Verify and document the webhook deployment path
tasks.details:
Plan: docs/development-deployment-plan.md#t117-verify-and-document-the-webhook-deployment-path

The signed GitHub push webhook is already configured and tested. This task makes its verification and maintenance repeatable rather than recreating it.

Acceptance: The audit distinguishes an enabled switch from a working webhook. An explicit signed test can prove the path through a finished deployment and matching revision, with no duplicate manual rollout.
steps: Document the current main-branch deployment path, secret ownership, rotation procedure, and location of GitHub delivery and Coolify deployment records.
Add a read-only configuration audit for webhook activity, push subscription, destination, signature-secret presence, main branch selection, and auto-deploy setting. Never display the secret.
Provide an explicit end-to-end test mode that replays a selected GitHub delivery or uses the supported test endpoint. Identify the commit and warn that this mode starts a deployment.
Correlate delivery outcome, Coolify deployment, installed revision, and verification results. Do not queue a manual deployment while the webhook deployment is running.

Test invalid signatures, other branches, delivery failure, missing webhook configuration, and duplicate delivery behavior in an isolated setup. Use the live test only during an authorized deployment window.
